entries.label: Oathbound Reconciliation
entries.description: Reconciliation after bitter division is a source of public legitimacy. Keeping a sovereign's conciliatory oath, sustaining cooperation, and repairing distrust are admired as achievements that hostility alone cannot secure. An oath gains substance when former opponents can share a decision without having every old injury called settled. The leader who listens to an inconvenient grievance, keeps a difficult promise, and makes cooperation bear fruit gives reconciliation something sturdier than a magnificent speech. The inherited ideal does not establish a new treaty or friendship in the present encounter.
entries.rationale: Retains the mod-specific conciliatory ideal without asserting a particular ruler's history or a current peace settlement. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Adaptable Skirmish Warfare
entries.description: Effective fighting means adjusting light troops to unfamiliar ground rather than insisting on one favored battlefield. Scouts, flexible deployments, and practical responses to changing conditions earn military respect. A scout's report can deserve more attention than the commander's favorite plan. Respect belongs to finding a workable approach, keeping lightly equipped companions useful, and recognizing when an unfamiliar obstacle has changed what courage requires. This is an established tactical preference, not universal personal training.
entries.rationale: Authored adaptable skirmish warfare reading of the fingerprinted definition. entries.label: Agrarian Foundations
entries.description: Cultivation and the households that sustain it form the basis of prosperity and military provisioning. Abundant food can support many levies, while comfortable agricultural life offers less encouragement to the hardiness prized in harsher lands. The grain brought safely into storage gives a boast about military strength its practical foundation. A prosperous household can take pride in a dependable season, generous provision, and the comfort its labor allows others to enjoy, even when fighters mock that comfort as softness. Public usefulness need not be measured by a warrior's ambition.
entries.rationale: Authored agrarian foundations reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Inherited Mining Knowledge
entries.description: Recognizing valuable seams and opening workable excavations are respected forms of inherited expertise. Ore and gems reward patient knowledge of stone as much as physical labor. Experienced judgment notices the seam an impatient newcomer passes, the change in stone that deserves another look, and the support whose neglect would cost companions their return. Bringing ore and people home gives inherited expertise an achievement others can understand. Mining experience supplies cultural confidence without placing a mine, deposit, or mineral fortune in the current scene.
entries.rationale: Authored inherited mining knowledge reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Inherited Craftsmanship
entries.description: A trade is often learned within a family, with successive generations refining the same techniques. A craftsperson's reputation can carry the work of predecessors as well as present skill. The clean meeting of fitted surfaces, a dependable handle, or a finish that rewards close inspection gives a family name substance. A teacher passes on the method behind the admired object; a pupil's improvement can honor that inheritance while testing how generously it was entrusted. Continuity makes careful teaching and dependable workmanship matters of household standing.
entries.rationale: Authored inherited craftsmanship reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Prestige through Negotiation
entries.description: Compelling an opponent to yield without a battle is regarded as the purest expression of superiority. Wars cannot be declared against allies or parties protected by a truce. Persuasion, bargaining, and understanding another party's interests can display superiority more elegantly than force. A rival persuaded to accept a difficult term gives the negotiator an achievement worth retelling. Reading the other party's need, offering something they can defend before their companions, and securing a promise that survives the meeting make clever words answerable to results. A successful settlement can therefore carry real prestige rather than appear a consolation for weakness.
entries.rationale: Authored prestige through negotiation reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact. Source-strength clarification: The adopted description treats compelling an enemy to yield without fighting as the purest expression of superiority. Restores that prestige priority; exact cannot_attack_allies/cannot_attack_truces parameters prohibit declaring war against allies or parties protected by a truce; installed declare_war_interaction confirms this exact scope, without a universal ban on every interpersonal harm.

entries.label: War for Material Gain
entries.description: War is judged by what its participants can acquire and afford, with captured wealth taking precedence over splendid reputation. A campaign that produces honors but leaves its fighters unable to pay their costs can seem foolish. A captured chest has to pay for repairs, provisions, and the people who expect their share. Splendid titles lose their shine when they leave a fighter poorer; bargaining over the spoils can expose the difference between a profitable campaign and a leader's expensive vanity. This outlook supplies a material justification for plunder, not an observed act of theft.
entries.rationale: Authored war for material gain reading of the fingerprinted definition. entries.label: Brewing and Fellowship
entries.description: Making and sharing alcoholic drink belong to familiar daily sociability as well as celebration. Brewing skill, a welcome drink, and company around it can express attachment and local pride. A recipe remembered, a batch watched patiently, and a cup chosen for someone else's taste turn workmanship into fellowship. The maker's best praise can be companions lingering over what was shared, while a novel flavor gives a traveler something worth bringing home. The custom gives drink social meaning without making every member intoxicated or willing to partake. Eligible city holdings may build the brewery line through this custom. Farm-and-field and manor-house lines add county approval where the local culture retains the enabling practice.
entries.rationale: Authored brewing and fellowship reading of the fingerprinted definition. entries.label: Armed Conversion
entries.rationale: Excluded from cultural steering because armed propagation of belief and divine approval are the defining teaching. A secular martial substitute would discard that meaning; the relevant religious context belongs to the faith domain.

entries.label: Imperial Court Protocol
entries.description: Courtly conduct is governed by an intricate inherited imperial etiquette. Knowing when to speak, how to acknowledge rank, and how ceremony expresses legitimacy can matter as much as a direct claim to authority. A greeting offered too early or a seat accepted too readily can reveal how little a visitor understands precedence. Those who know the etiquette can recognize an insult hidden within impeccable courtesy, or grant an adversary dignity without surrendering their own claim. Formal refinement can conceal competition without proving that a particular court or intrigue is present.
entries.rationale: Retains elaborate imperial protocol while removing the reused Eastern Roman historical setting. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Caravan Commerce
entries.description: Traveling commerce is a familiar basis of livelihood and reputation. Moving goods between communities requires dependable arrangements, practical route knowledge, and sustained relationships with buyers and suppliers. A dependable contact at the next stop can be worth more than a splendid bargain with someone who disappears afterward. Reputation travels with goods: the promise kept during a difficult crossing and the damaged consignment honestly accounted for teach distant partners whom to trust. Cultural association with caravan trade does not make the speaker a merchant or establish a caravan nearby.
entries.rationale: Authored caravan commerce reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Fortified Security
entries.description: Security is sought through a dense foundation of strongholds rather than confidence in attack alone. Building and maintaining fortified places are valued as lasting investments in defense. A gate maintained before it fails and provisions considered before danger arrives make protection a continuing craft. The builder who understands an overlooked approach can earn lasting esteem, while a ruler's magnificent new walls invite questions about who will keep them sound. The ideal describes how protection is imagined, without supplying an existing castle or construction project.
entries.rationale: Authored fortified security reading of the fingerprinted definition. entries.label: Purifying Water Rites
entries.rationale: Excluded because water's ritual purification is the defining meaning. Replacing it with ordinary cleanliness would invent a secular teaching that the source does not establish.

entries.label: Care for the Less Fortunate
entries.description: Helping those with fewer resources is a public good in its own right, rather than a favor reserved for people sharing the same beliefs. Willingness to support the vulnerable can earn esteem across community boundaries. A useful gift notices what lets another person keep living with dignity: provisions, repaired shelter, patient attention, or room among familiar company. Generosity has a revealing cost when the recipient cannot return the favor or belongs to a household the giver dislikes. Available resources and a person's actual choices still determine what aid occurs.
entries.rationale: Authored care for the less fortunate reading of the fingerprinted definition. entries.label: Chivalric Conduct
entries.description: Accomplished fighting is expected to answer to duty, honorable conduct, and a cultivated reputation. Romantic literature and poetic courtship share that social ideal with martial excellence. A warrior's manner is judged beside the deed: whether the vulnerable were protected, a promise honored, and a rival answered without petty humiliation. Verse and courtship give the same reputation a gentler audience, where elegance can express care or merely advertise the speaker. Courtesy may express conviction or polish an ambitious image; the tradition itself supplies no sworn order or personal vow.
entries.rationale: Authored chivalric conduct reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Urban Civic Pride
entries.description: Great cities are understood as the centers of collective achievement. Their development and distinction can become matters of cultural pride, making urban improvement more than a ruler's private convenience. A well-kept passage, a useful public work, and an achievement visitors remember give inhabitants something to claim together. Civic pride can rejoice in another person's improvement or turn possessive when newcomers use the city in ways its admirers never planned. This esteem does not establish the size, prosperity, or condition of any particular settlement.
entries.rationale: Authored urban civic pride reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Unsettled Common Outlook
entries.description: Unusual perceptions and erratic judgments are familiar within the community's shared outlook. Explanations may appeal to inherited nature or collective suffering, but neither cause is established for a particular person. A story ordinary listeners find bewildering can receive a familiar answer at home. Shared eccentricity gives companionship to unusual experience, while competing accounts of what happened can make trust and judgment difficult; recognition need not mean that every strange conclusion is accepted. This gives eccentric conduct a cultural setting without diagnosing everyone or assigning a clinical condition.
entries.rationale: Preserves the source's unsettling collective tendency without repeating its dismissive wording or fabricating trauma, symptoms, or a universal diagnosis. entries.label: Land as a Common Trust
entries.description: Land is understood as belonging to the people collectively rather than as an individual's private possession. Its use should serve shared needs, and exclusive claims can appear to deny an obligation to the wider community. The question is what the ground can sustain for everyone who depends on it. A household's careful work can deserve recognition without making the place its exclusive prize, and a prosperous claimant may be asked whose labor and needs made that prosperity possible. This is a customary conception of ownership, not proof of an enacted land law.
entries.rationale: Authored land as a common trust reading of the fingerprinted definition. entries.label: Recognized Concubinage
entries.description: Rulers commonly maintain recognized companions alongside formal marriage. Such households have an established cultural place even where the prevailing belief system would prefer a different arrangement. Recognition gives companions a place in household expectations that secrecy alone would not provide. Affection, access, jealousy, and responsibility can make that place consequential, while the person honored by public acknowledgment can still dispute what the household expects from them. The custom establishes social familiarity, not the speaker's partners or consent to any proposed relationship.
entries.rationale: Authored recognized concubinage reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Trusted Court Eunuchs
entries.description: Eunuchs are familiar participants in household service, administration, and military leadership. They are often considered particularly trustworthy because court opinion associates their condition with freedom from certain intimate ambitions. An official entrusted with private business can acquire influence through reliability and long familiarity with the household. Public confidence may open doors while reducing the person to an assumed absence of ambition; a discerning patron must still notice the actual judgment behind the trusted position. That social assumption does not establish an individual's desires, loyalty, or competence.
entries.rationale: Retains actual eunuch roles and the community's trust rationale as a belief, not a factual assertion that eunuchs lack desire. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Food as Shared Art
entries.description: Food is both an art and a customary shared ceremony around which family and community gather; skilled preparation earns esteem beyond nourishment. Preparing and sharing food are valued as skilled expression and as a way to bring households and neighbors together. A meal can carry care, pride, and belonging beyond its nutritional purpose. Good preparation notices more than hunger: a guest's preference, an ingredient handled attentively, and the pleasure of serving something worth sharing. An unfamiliar method can delight a teacher or provoke a dispute over whether the cook understood the work behind the inherited recipe. This appreciation supplies no particular dish, feast, ingredient, or cooking ability. Feasts cost more; successful ones can earn extra prestige and dynasty renown. Eligible duchy-or-higher rulers may appoint a Food Taster; an appointee of this culture can perform better.

entries.label: Disciplined Inner Practice
entries.description: Training the body, regulating the breath, and steadying attention are understood as parts of improving one's character. Patient practice is esteemed over restless self-display. Repeated movement, measured breath, and attention to the next choice give composure a practiced foundation. The discipline is tested when affection, anger, or the wish to impress begins to direct a person who thought they had learned to command themselves. This embodied discipline does not establish supernatural attainment, a particular school, or the speaker's level of training.
entries.rationale: Retains the source's embodied self-cultivation without importing an external cosmology or treating practice as magical ability. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Proud Cultural Sufficiency
entries.description: The community considers its own inherited achievements and social life sufficient grounds for pride. Seeking approval or companionship outside that circle can seem unnecessary or demeaning. An inherited song or method can deserve affection without an outsider's applause. Pride becomes harder to distinguish from complacency when a useful unfamiliar idea is rejected because accepting it would mean admitting that the community has something left to learn. Such confidence can preserve identity while making unfamiliar customs harder to hear fairly.

entries.label: Everyday Cultural Exchange
entries.description: Living alongside other peoples has made borrowing languages, habits, and practical customs a familiar part of life. Incorporation can enrich a shared identity rather than simply replace it. A borrowed greeting, a useful tool, or a recipe changed through friendship can become part of ordinary belonging. People can disagree about what to keep while still recognizing the neighbor who first taught it; exchange gives inherited practice new company rather than one inevitable destination. Openness to exchange does not determine which elements have actually been adopted.

entries.label: Eclectic Public Customs
entries.description: Public habits contain conspicuous contrasts and shifting preferences. What one custom celebrates another may resist, making a single tidy account of the community unreliable. A visitor can earn praise for a gesture that another gathering would find ridiculous. People accustomed to those contrasts may be skilled at reading the company before speaking, while someone seeking a consistent rule can find familiar improvisation as frustrating as outsiders do. Familiarity with these contradictions can encourage improvisation without requiring an individual to behave unpredictably.

entries.label: Desert Travel with Camels
entries.description: Camel handling and knowledge of desert travel support movement, work, and warfare through severe dry country. The animals' care and practical value are part of the adopted way of life. A well-handled camel, a load balanced for distance, and knowledge of when to rest give the journey a dependable rhythm. The experienced traveler can admire patient care more than a boast about speed, knowing how quickly poor handling turns a companion animal into a liability. Retaining that specific craft does not locate the present encounter in a desert or give the speaker a mount.
entries.rationale: Keeps the source's actual camel tradition; no Warcraft mount species is substituted without supporting captured evidence. entries.label: Life around the Herd
entries.description: Tending horses and remaining close to the herd are valued above settled luxury. Attention to an animal's condition can be a mark of seriousness and belonging, while distant comfort may seem less rewarding than life in the saddle. A familiar horse's unsettled gait can draw closer attention than an offer of luxurious lodging. Quiet care before and after riding gives the bond its substance, and a fine rider's standing depends on what the animal can sustain as well as what the rider wants to display. Actual ownership and riding skill remain separate facts.

entries.label: Continuity in Exile
entries.description: Loss of a valued homeland gives preservation and rebuilding particular social weight. Dispersed communities can seek a place to begin again while keeping attachments to what was left behind. A recipe, remembered place-name, or carefully taught family method can keep an absent homeland particular. A new home offers safety and possibilities of its own, leaving elders and younger companions to decide which attachments can travel and which forms must change to keep them alive. The inherited experience does not supply the speaker's birthplace, journey, or personal memories.
entries.rationale: Authored continuity in exile reading of the fingerprinted definition. entries.label: Household Guard Tradition
entries.description: A ruler's trusted armed household provides both close protection and a core of heavy infantry. Service binds personal reliance to the wider work of defense. The close guard's reputation depends on being dependable when ceremony gives way to danger. Shared service builds knowledge of who will hold position and who notices the overlooked approach; intimacy with the ruler can bring pride as well as suspicion from those kept outside it. The tradition does not prove the presence of bodyguards or membership in a particular retinue.
entries.rationale: Removes the reused Varangian identity while retaining the source's dual bodyguard and infantry functions. entries.label: Dryland Livelihoods
entries.description: Finding water and making careful use of dry soil are respected practical skills. Familiarity with arid conditions supports settlement and cultivation where less experienced communities would struggle. A small change in ground, a reliable water source, and the timing of necessary work reward careful observation. Making scarce provision last can be an achievement a comfortable visitor fails to notice, until their own ambitious plan depends on the knowledge they dismissed. This is inherited environmental knowledge, not an observation of current drought or terrain.
entries.rationale: Authored dryland livelihoods reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Prestigious Falconry
entries.description: Breeding, training, and hunting with birds of prey are cultivated pursuits associated with high standing. Patience and skill in handling a raptor can make a pastime a visible accomplishment. The handler who attends to a fledgling, reads a raptor's response, and earns its return has something to show beyond an expensive bird. Quiet patience gives the hunt its accomplishment; careless display can reveal that the person boasting of mastery has learned little about the animal. This specific tradition does not grant a different flying creature, a familiar, or an owned bird.

entries.label: Restless Younger Nobles
entries.description: Younger noble sons are associated with mounted adventure, mercenary service, and attempts to win standing beyond the household. Their ambition can be audacious and unscrupulous, making distant opportunity attractive when inheritance offers little. A younger son can seek a name distant companions will recognize when the household's future seems reserved for someone else. A daring contract offers freedom and an audience, but the promise of distinction can make an unscrupulous patron's terms look more generous than they are. The pattern does not supply the speaker's birth order or exploits.

entries.label: Exclusive Cosmopolitan Refinement
entries.description: Luxurious refinement and cultivated public life are treated as evidence of superiority. The community admires its own cosmopolitan achievements while dismissing challenges from outside its favored sphere. Dress, accomplished conversation, and discriminating taste give refinement a public language. The admirer who notices a difficult artistic choice offers gratifying company; the host who mistakes an unfamiliar manner for ignorance can miss the insight the visitor came to bring. Welcoming sophistication and contempt for unfamiliar people can therefore coexist.
entries.rationale: Authored exclusive cosmopolitan refinement reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Prestige of Disciplined Regiments
entries.description: Elite armored regiments prize disciplined service and the reputation of their units over a noble warrior's isolated display of courage. Collective identity gives accomplishment a continuing audience. A regiment keeps memories of coordinated work, discipline under pressure, and companions whose reliability made success possible. An isolated flourish may win applause elsewhere while earning criticism within the unit if others had to abandon their task to recover the daring fighter. A daring act can be judged poorly if it sacrifices formation or the unit's standing.
entries.rationale: Removes reused historical regiment names while retaining organized military pride and contempt for reckless personal glory. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Proud Highland Nobility
entries.description: Mounted nobles from strong upland households guard their dignity intensely. A public insult can outlast a bodily wound in the community's memory, making words politically costly. A slight offered before familiar witnesses can challenge the standing of an entire household. A measured answer may preserve dignity better than immediate violence, but rivals can make patience costly by retelling it as submission; the audience becomes part of the wound. This inherited reputation does not establish an actual feud or demand revenge from every individual.
entries.rationale: Replaces the external noble-class name with its supported martial and honor-based social meaning. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Advancement through Palace Patronage
entries.description: Court service joins elaborate honors and cultivated display to a substantial political apparatus. Eunuchs, flatterers, and other ambitious officials can pursue advancement through access and favor. A title, invitation, or remembered introduction can signal whose counsel has acquired a hearing. Accomplished service and flattering display compete for recognition, while the person who opens a door can expect their own favor remembered when the next appointment is discussed. Apparent refinement need not reveal the rivalries beneath it, but no particular plot follows from the custom.
entries.rationale: Authored advancement through palace patronage reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Ceremonial Imperial Legitimacy
entries.description: Inherited imperial ceremony gives the ruling office grandeur and makes public recognition of authority socially important. Spectacle and reverence can coexist with unrest rather than guarantee willing obedience. A procession or formal acknowledgment can make authority visible to people who seldom meet its holder. Grandeur gives the office continuity beyond one incumbent, while those expected to applaud can judge how much the ruler's conduct deserves the dignity the ceremony lends. The custom supplies an idiom of legitimacy without introducing an external empire or historical emperor.
entries.rationale: Removes Roman identity while retaining ceremonial grandeur, awe for office, and public tension. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Broadly Shared Inheritance
entries.description: Dividing a ruler's lands among children has an established place, including children whom narrower customs would exclude. Family claims can therefore be discussed through a wider expectation of participation. A younger child's claim can have an audience beside the household's expected heir. Sharing the inheritance asks how to preserve useful cooperation when several children can imagine a future in the same lands; affectionate promises become difficult when division has a real cost. Equal gender succession may be enacted; this permission establishes no current law. When the current broad gender teaching favors one sex, rulers of the other meet less disapproval.
entries.rationale: Authored broadly shared inheritance reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Esteem for Impartial Judgment
entries.description: Honest accounts and judgments that treat competing parties fairly are publicly valued. Influence should answer to the merits of a dispute rather than simply to the stronger household. A careful hearing notices whose account has been drowned out by rank or force. Esteem belongs to a judgment the losing party can understand even while resenting it, and to the willingness to apply the same standard when one's own household stands to benefit. The ideal supplies a standard by which conduct is judged, not an assurance that every judgment achieves it.
entries.rationale: Authored esteem for impartial judgment reading of the fingerprinted definition. entries.label: Prestige through Welcoming Guests
entries.description: Rulers are expected to welcome anyone who comes to their court generously and make hospitality a spectacular accomplishment. An impressive welcome can honor a guest while displaying the host's resources and standing. A welcome is remembered through attention as well as expense: a place offered generously, a preference noticed, an introduction that gives the guest standing. The ruler's display earns deeper admiration when it honors someone who brings no profitable favor in return. The expectation does not establish that guests, servants, or a banquet are presently assembled.
entries.rationale: Authored prestige through welcoming guests reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Public expectation supplies no assembled court, actual guest, enforceable access right, safe conduct or automatic personal compliance.

entries.label: Enduring Grievance
entries.description: Injury and insult are expected to be remembered rather than readily forgiven. Answering a slight can defend personal and collective standing, while leaving it unanswered may invite contempt. A cheerful gathering need not mean an old injury has been forgiven. Remembering the exact slight gives a claim continuity, while companions may disagree over whether its answer protects standing or burdens another generation with a quarrel it did not begin. The custom gives retaliation social weight without supplying a grievance or forcing an individual's response.

entries.label: Belief-Based Succession Eligibility
entries.description: Succession is reserved for members of the community's recognized belief group. Difference in belief can disqualify an otherwise suitable heir, making public membership politically consequential. An heir's public affiliation can matter as much as aptitude or closeness of blood. A household may admire a capable relative while questioning whether that person belongs within the recognized circle, making a change of professed belief carry consequences beyond private conviction. This is a cultural eligibility norm; the enacted succession law still requires observation.

entries.label: Family Enterprises
entries.description: Businesses commonly develop through successive generations of the same household. Inherited tools, practical knowledge, and a dependable family reputation give enterprise a durable social foundation. Tools and contacts can carry the memory of the person who first made the enterprise dependable. A successor inherits expectations along with opportunities; improving the work can honor the family name while unsettling relatives who understood loyalty as doing it their way. A successor may be expected to sustain that work without being assumed to own a business personally. Close relatives serving on councils or in court positions gain advantages in their work; revoking close kin's titles costs public prestige. This establishes no actual appointment, personal competence or title.

entries.label: Customary Female Preeminence
entries.description: Women hold the predominant place within the customary ruling hierarchy. That public prominence can shape ordinary expectations about family standing, authority, and whose leadership appears familiar. A woman's command can sound ordinary rather than exceptional, and her judgment can shape familiar expectations about household standing and leadership. Skill earns recognition within those expectations, while men in respected positions can show how custom and individual accomplishment coexist. entries.label: Frequent Communal Celebration
entries.description: Frequent exuberant celebrations have a valued place in common life, even when outsiders call their frequency and display vulgar. Music, good food, and an excuse to gather give even a modest accomplishment a generous audience. Outsiders may call the noise excessive; companions can recognize the affection in remembering who deserves a turn at the center of the celebration. The custom supplies a social disposition toward festivity, not a festival occurring in the current scene. Eligible feasts and camp parties can recur sooner; reveler lifestyles are more common and carry added public prestige.

entries.label: Accomplished Fishing Communities
entries.description: Rare fishing mastery is admired through an ideal of bountiful catches whatever the tide or wind, and knowledge of coast, land and sea that no rival surpasses. Dependable catches express accumulated expertise rather than luck alone. The promising tide is read beside weather, equipment, and what the households waiting ashore will need. An elder's warning can be worth more than a younger fisher's magnificent boast, and a dependable return gives knowledge an achievement that others can share. Cultural confidence in the craft does not guarantee a particular catch or make every member a fisher.

entries.label: Patience under Hardship
entries.description: Keeping one's composure through difficulty is familiar and esteemed. Endurance can express strength without immediate retaliation or dramatic complaint. A restrained answer can leave another person's anger room to pass without surrendering the matter under dispute. Endurance acquires weight through repeated inconvenience, with the person who waits still entitled to remember what the delay costs them. The shared habit makes restraint intelligible within the community while leaving impatience and anger available to particular people.

entries.label: Woodland Combat Knowledge
entries.description: Understanding obstructed sightlines and difficult movement in woodland is a recognized military advantage. Familiarity with forest fighting gives planning and practical experience a place alongside force. A narrow approach, broken sightline, and unexpected obstruction can reward the fighter who listens before advancing. Coordination depends on noticing where companions can move and where a larger force will lose its advantage, giving local judgment a victory brute strength cannot guarantee. entries.label: Woodland Livelihoods
entries.description: Gathering usable resources from woodland is a familiar foundation of life. Knowing what the forest can provide rewards accumulated observation and practical skill. Knowledge includes what can be gathered safely, what deserves time to grow again, and how useful materials behave once brought home. A careful repair or dependable provision can show more understanding than a traveler loudly admiring the trees without knowing what they sustain. entries.label: Inherited Woodland Defense
entries.description: Woodland experience is valued as a means of protecting an inherited homeland. Knowledge passed between generations can make defense a matter of belonging as well as military technique. The custom also limits contact with peoples it regards as lesser. A remembered path and a warning taught to the next watcher give defense continuity beyond a celebrated battle. The quiet work earns substance through people able to rest behind it; inherited confidence is tested when a new threat arrives by an unfamiliar approach. The defensive ideal does not establish a present invasion or the character's current surroundings.

entries.label: Coordinated Battle Formations
entries.description: Military effectiveness is sought through formations that allow different troop types to protect and reinforce one another. Timing and mutual reliability can be admired above isolated prowess. A fighter's timing matters to the companions whose movement depends on it. Holding an assigned place can deserve more praise than chasing an isolated prize, and a commander earns trust through understanding how different troops make one another useful. entries.label: Terrain-Aware Defense
entries.description: Protecting the homeland combines defensive construction, knowledge of local ground, archery, and mobile troops. Ingenuity can compensate for an opponent's strength by shaping how an attack unfolds. A defended approach joins the wall, the ground outside it, the archer's sightline, and the route a mobile force can use. Ingenious protection gives a smaller community something to rely on, while an overlooked weakness can expose how little a splendid design understood daily needs. These are complementary defensive crafts, not proof of any particular fortification or engagement.

entries.label: Martial Life by the Sea
entries.description: The shoreline is associated with familiar livelihood, freedom, and martial identity. Coastal experience gives service and adventure a distinctive appeal that inland comfort may not replace. A familiar coast gives martial pride memories of departure and return as well as danger. Skill learned through ordinary work can matter in a difficult landing, and the fighter tempted by distant adventure remains someone companions hope to see come home. entries.label: Reputation through Stories
entries.description: Life is understood through the stories told about deeds and people. A telling can preserve an achievement, alter a reputation, or determine what later generations remember. A deed acquires another life in the version others keep telling. The omitted companion, the inconvenient failure, and the boast remembered by a rival can change standing as much as the original success; a fine account therefore deserves an audience willing to question it. Words about conduct therefore carry social weight alongside the conduct itself.

entries.label: Honor Proven in Public
entries.description: Standing is continually gained or lost through visible deeds and the handling of insults. An established warrior can sink in esteem while an unproven youth rises through an admired response. An earned name or celebrated exploit gives the bearer something to answer for before familiar witnesses. A daring act that brings companions home can deserve more admiration than a reckless success bought with their lives, even when the latter makes a louder story. Public judgment can pressure conduct without ensuring every challenge is accepted.

Recognition can change how familiar companions speak to someone once dismissed, while the person guarding entry must decide whether a failed attempt proves incapacity or merely reveals what still needs teaching. entries.label: Combat as Judgment
entries.description: A weapons contest is regarded as faster, fairer justice than pleading before distrusted law and magistrates; words can be dismissed as cowardice. Crimes may be settled by single combat against someone the claimant cannot imprison and who is not their liege. Victory can be treated as a claim to justice. Witnesses can measure who held the field more readily than they can untangle a magistrate's argument. The apparent clarity gives the winner standing, while the defeated party's continued resentment tests how completely a visible contest can settle an invisible claim. entries.label: Pragmatic Life under Changing Rulers
entries.description: Learning to live under different rulers is treated as a practical form of freedom. A change in a sovereign's origin need not determine whether ordinary life remains workable. A household can judge a new ruler by whether useful work and ordinary obligations remain possible. Knowing how to make a request heard under unfamiliar authority can preserve more freedom than a grand declaration that leaves the speaker's dependents exposed. Accommodation can reflect resourcefulness rather than heartfelt loyalty or approval.

entries.label: Friendship beyond Kinship

Shared sociability can turn friendship into an enduring bond with its own expectations of care and loyalty. The companion who knows an earlier failure can offer care different from the family's expectations. Shared pleasure gives the bond a beginning; keeping a difficult promise gives it endurance, particularly when friendship and inherited duty ask for different choices. entries.label: Responsibility for Captured Soldiers
entries.description: A ruler who asks soldiers to risk captivity is expected to help secure their return, including those of low station. Protection after capture makes service a reciprocal obligation rather than a sacrifice demanded only from subordinates. A common soldier's return can measure the ruler's promises more exactly than another triumphal speech. Families remember whether rank determined who was worth recovering, and future volunteers can judge their own risk by what happened to those who served before them. entries.label: Strategic Games as Practice
entries.description: Simulated contests and games are valued as ways to keep judgment sharp. A commander should cultivate planning rather than rely on a fortunate outcome in battle. A harmless loss gives a player time to ask where the plan went wrong before lives depend on it. The companion who spots a neglected response can deserve respect without holding the highest rank; a commander who cannot bear that correction wastes the exercise's best lesson. entries.label: Shared Scientific Learning

Accomplished inquiry can earn wider social esteem rather than merely serve a court. A surprising result, an elegant explanation, and a method another thinker can improve give discovery its public pleasure. Learning from several traditions asks the admired scholar to hear the unfamiliar idea that unsettles a cherished answer. The adopted ideal does not make every member a scholar.

entries.label: Learned and Cultivated Rule

Seeking capable counsel can honor the same ideal when personal skill is lacking. A well-turned verse can display attention, while a sound decision proves whether that attention reaches the people governed. A ruler honors learning by hearing an inconvenient adviser, rather than collecting accomplished companions merely to decorate their own reputation. entries.label: Resilient Independence
entries.description: Remaining self-governing despite attempts at domination is central to public identity. Resilience and military accomplishment can make dependence feel costly even when an outsider promises comfort. A repaired defense and a decision made among one's own people can carry pride beyond their material value. Offers of protection are weighed against who will gain the right to decide next, leaving comfort attractive without making dependence inexpensive. entries.label: Worth of the Ordinary Soldier

entries.label: Practical Armor for Many

entries.label: Work for the Community

entries.label: Inherited Feudal Standing

entries.label: Highland Fighting Traditions
entries.description: Military practice values familiarity with sloping ground, valleys, and upland approaches. Knowing how difficult terrain shapes movement can count as a serious martial advantage. An uphill advance, a sheltered approach, or a valley that constrains pursuit changes the meaning of a brave plan. Experienced judgment knows where strength will tire and where a smaller force can remain useful, making attention to ground part of martial pride. entries.label: Hillside Livelihoods

The visitor impressed only by hardship can overlook the ingenuity that makes an uneven place a dependable home. entries.label: Esteem for Productive Cultivators
entries.description: A substantial farming population is valued for sustaining everyone whose work lies elsewhere. Accumulated knowledge supports intensive cultivation of wheat or rice according to what local conditions suit. The labor that makes an abundant field dependable can be overlooked by people admiring the city or army it feeds. Careful cultivators know which method the land will bear, and their standing gains substance when the wider community acknowledges the patience behind its comfort. Military and urban success depend on cultivators, without asserting an actual harvest or making every member a farmer.

entries.label: Preference for Internal Affairs
entries.description: The community prefers to keep its attention and relationships within its own familiar sphere. Outside ties can seem intrusive or less useful than tending established concerns. A familiar household or local concern can feel more deserving of time than an outsider's urgent invitation. Keeping distance preserves attention for what is already valued, while a visitor who understands those obligations may receive a better hearing than one demanding immediate enthusiasm. That preference describes social distance rather than a universally hostile response to every visitor. Marriage across cultures meets reluctance; idle courtiers tend to remain with rulers sharing their culture. Adopting local culture can be stressful. Epidemics enter its lands less readily, without establishing personal immunity.

entries.description: Military practice values the ability to move through tangled growth and difficult tropical approaches. Familiarity with those obstacles can make positioning and passage more important than a straightforward advance. Broken visibility and tangled passage give movement a different rhythm from an open advance. The companion who can choose a workable approach and keep others together may be more valuable than the strongest fighter impatiently clearing a conspicuous path. entries.label: Defensive Archery
entries.description: The bow is an established means of defending communities against raiders and brigands. Familiarity with archery gives protection a recognizable practical craft, rather than merely a boast of strength. A bowmaker's careful work, dependable practice, and a warning carried in time give the defender's shot its purpose. Protection earns standing through the community kept safe, with patient preparation deserving attention beside the moment everyone remembers. The tradition does not make every member an archer or establish the present terrain.

entries.label: Esteem for Learning Languages
entries.description: Learning another community's language is an esteemed accomplishment. Attending to unfamiliar words can open understanding that translation or assumption alone would miss. A greeting understood on its own terms can open a conversation that a rough translation would have closed. The careful learner notices the distinction that carries respect, humor, or offense, and admits uncertainty before turning an unfamiliar word into an easy assumption. The cultural value of study does not confer fluency or identify a language the speaker actually knows.

entries.label: Authority of Codified Law
entries.description: Codified law and its rule are regarded as the foremost measure of a civilized society, with a community expected to make its rules explicit and treat them as a governing standard. Written and organized law can command respect beyond a ruler's immediate preference. A promise gains weight when the same rule can be explained to the powerful and the inconvenient petitioner. An exact agreement can give cooperation substance without friendship, while a precisely lawful decision can leave an individual questioning whether the governing standard is adequate. The teaching does not establish whether others welcome, suppress or punish that disagreement. This esteem does not supply a legal text, enacted law, or fair application in a particular dispute.

entries.description: Freedom from the Scourge gives collective identity a fierce attachment to regained will and hostility toward former masters. Long undeath can preserve grievances and diminish the customary value placed on life. A familiar song or craft can become something reclaimed for a purpose no former master commands. entries.label: Defiant Gallows Humor
entries.description: Meeting danger and even death with laughter is culturally admired. A joke can deny an enemy the satisfaction of visible fear and make life's uncertainty bearable through irreverence. The sharp answer can give companions a way to face what reassurance cannot make harmless. A laugh may be affectionate, furious, or grieving; the hearer who understands it can recognize courage without mistaking the joke for indifference. entries.label: Inherited Self-Preservation
entries.description: Keeping well is treated as inherited knowledge that may be developed within the community or learned from long-lived peoples. Patient care and caution carry public value because they help preserve life through illness and hardship. A sensible routine, a warning heeded, and knowledge passed on before it is lost give preservation a patient form. Admiration for long life can make a young person's impatience seem careless, while an elder's own habits remain open to improvement. entries.label: Unqualified Cultural Nonviolence
entries.description: Using force is regarded as unjustifiable, including when others describe it as necessary. Peace is understood as something sustained by refusing violence rather than by winning a final battle. Refusal can become costly when someone offers safety on condition that the community accepts force. The demanding ideal asks how disputes and fear will be answered without making violence the final argument, with patience and practical protection needing forms people can sustain. This is the community's demanding ideal; an individual's conduct and disagreement remain separately established.
entries.rationale: Preserves the cultural source's absolute rejection of force, distinct from the faith pacifism tenet's whenever-possible formulation. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Competitive Local Civic Pride
entries.description: Urban communities prize their independence and compete to make their own city more distinguished than its neighbors. Investment and civic energy can express local attachment as well as rivalry. A better-kept street or a work admired by visitors can become a victory over the neighboring city. Local enthusiasm gives improvement a willing audience, while rivalry can make a useful borrowed method difficult to acknowledge without losing face. The custom supplies no present dispute, public work, or particular city's prosperity.
entries.rationale: Authored competitive local civic pride reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Open-Country Herding
entries.description: Keeping substantial herds in wide open country is an established livelihood. Knowledge of animals and the land that supports them can carry practical and social importance. A healthy herd, an overlooked water need, and grazing that will remain useful give foresight a practical measure. An experienced keeper's warning can defend tomorrow's provision against today's tempting gain, with attachment extending to companions whose work keeps the animals dependable. The tradition does not establish a current herd, a moving camp, or the speaker's occupation.
entries.rationale: Authored open-country herding reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Thought and Self-Examination
entries.description: Careful thought and examination of one's own assumptions are encouraged as worthwhile pursuits. A considered account can earn esteem alongside a useful action. The admired thinker asks what a comfortable answer assumed and whom that assumption leaves unheard. A careful argument can carry affection or severity; esteem belongs to examining the reasoning rather than merely repeating the name of someone known to be wise. The shared value does not guarantee wisdom, assign an education, or make every exchange a philosophical argument.
entries.rationale: Authored thought and self-examination reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Poetry as Accomplishment
entries.description: Shaping language into meaningful verse is regarded as a cultivated and honorable art. A poem can earn recognition for the quality of its expression, rather than only for the power of its author. An exact image or an unexpected turn gives a familiar feeling a new audience. The listener who notices how a difficult line works offers praise deeper than admiration for the poet's title, while an inherited verse can acquire meaning its maker never intended. The custom establishes neither a work already composed nor a speaker's poetic ability.
entries.rationale: Authored poetry as accomplishment reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Multiple-Spouse Households
entries.description: Maintaining more than one spouse is a familiar cultural arrangement even where a belief system would favor another pattern. Household relationships can therefore be discussed without assuming exclusive partnership is the only respectable form. Recognized partnerships give affection more than one public place in household expectations. Attention, time, and practical responsibility can become questions the partners must negotiate, with familiarity of the arrangement unable to settle another person's wishes for them. No actual marriage, partner, or consent follows from membership.
entries.rationale: Authored multiple-spouse households reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Profit through Maritime Raiding
entries.description: Attacking ports and taking their goods are recognized ways to gain wealth even when regarded as dishonorable. Practical profit can outweigh concern for a respectable reputation. A rich port's goods are judged by how much they will bring, rather than by how honorable their taking sounds. The share carried home can make a disreputable success persuasive, while losses and divided spoils expose whose risks paid for whose profit. The custom supplies neither a present raid nor a ship, victim, or pirate vocation.
entries.rationale: Authored profit through maritime raiding reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Frequent Territorial Quarrels
entries.description: Border disputes and opportunistic transfers of land are familiar parts of political life. Claims can be pursued aggressively without satisfying impartial standards of justice. An ambiguous boundary can become an opportunity for a claimant who thinks the neighbor unable to answer. Retelling the dispute gives each household reasons to defend its version, while those depending on shared routes must live with ambitions that make ordinary cooperation harder. This customary contentiousness does not establish a current war or make every individual personally argumentative.
entries.rationale: Authored frequent territorial quarrels reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Borrowed Worship Traditions
entries.rationale: Excluded because adopting elements of other groups' worship is the defining practice. Ordinary cultural exchange has its own separate concept and cannot substitute for this religious meaning.

entries.label: Patronage for Redemption
entries.rationale: Excluded because works offered for salvation and priestly praise are the defining motive. Secular public generosity would erase the distinctive religious relationship.

entries.label: Urban Participation in Government
entries.description: Urban classes have a recognized claim to political importance alongside rural landholders. Government is understood through a history of civic participation rather than landed rank alone. An accomplished town household can expect its contribution to deserve a political hearing beside landed power. The memory of civic participation gives a complaint a language of standing, while influential citizens can still disagree about whose useful work counts as a voice. The tradition does not establish an active republic, election, or an individual's formal rights.
entries.rationale: Authored urban participation in government reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Lasting Honor for Wounded Veterans
entries.description: Those who can no longer fight because of injury remain honored for their service. Their experience can give them a respected place as teachers rather than make them disposable. A former fighter's advice can preserve the knowledge that younger companions have yet to earn. Honoring service means giving the injured person a continuing place, with patient attention and meaningful work carrying more substance than praise offered only on ceremonial occasions. The ideal supplies no injury or service history for a particular person.
entries.rationale: Authored lasting honor for wounded veterans reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Rule across Cultural Divisions
entries.description: A governing group is accustomed to exercising power over subjects of another culture. Experience in suppressing revolt supports control while exposing rulers to distrust and resentment. A governing household can become practiced at hearing a subject's useful report while distrusting their claim to equal standing. Familiar control gives authority confidence, but cooperation obtained through fear can hide the knowledge a ruler most needs to keep the realm workable. This political pattern does not establish the speaker's position or an actual rebellion.
entries.rationale: Authored rule across cultural divisions reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Public Stone Commemoration
entries.description: Durable carved markers commemorate deaths, conquests, and advances in standing. Making a life's achievements visible can preserve family reputation beyond its immediate witnesses. An inscription chooses which deed survives after its witnesses are gone. A carved name can give descendants pride and a rival grounds for correction, leaving the durable monument dependent on the honesty and care of the account it preserves. The custom does not supply a particular inscription, conquest, monument, or magical property.
entries.rationale: Retains commemorative markers without assigning a terrestrial people or treating runic carving as enchantment. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Care for Living Woodland
entries.description: Woodland is treated as a living whole deserving care rather than as expendable material alone. Preserving trees can express responsibility toward a place that sustains community life. Care notices how a path, food source, growing tree, and animal's range affect one another. Selective clearing can serve the living whole, while an impressive refusal to touch anything can fail to understand what the woodland actually needs. This scoped cultural meaning does not establish a grove at the meeting place or every member's personal attachment.
entries.rationale: Retains the clearly separable forest-care ethic; tree sanctity and religious claims belong to independent faith evidence. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Devotional Mastery through Hunting
entries.rationale: Excluded because connection with the divine through hunting defines the concept. Ordinary hunting skill cannot replace that religious purpose without duplicating a different tradition.

entries.label: Revered Mountain Sanctity
entries.rationale: Excluded because mountains as connections to the divine are its defining meaning. Practical upland knowledge is covered separately and does not preserve this teaching.

entries.label: Long-Distance Desert Connections
entries.description: Experienced desert travelers connect distant settled regions across difficult open country. Route knowledge makes movement and exchange possible where unfamiliar travelers may see only separation. A reliable stopping place and a promise kept at the far end of a crossing give route knowledge a social life. The traveler can connect people who imagine themselves separated, carrying news, goods, and the memory of who made the difficult passage possible. The tradition supplies no particular terrestrial desert, current journey, or personally known route.
entries.rationale: Removes Sahara, Mediterranean, and Sahel geography while preserving experienced desert travel and interregional connection. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Authority of Educated Officials
entries.description: Loyal officials educated in cultivated arts are considered fitting holders of influence. Government can be judged by informed counsel and accomplished expression as well as military power. Cultivated expression matters most when it helps explain a decision to the people affected. An informed adviser can honor service by correcting a convenient account, while the official admired for learning must still hear the practical worker who knows what the plan overlooked. The shared ideal does not establish a person's office, education, or loyalty.
entries.rationale: Authored authority of educated officials reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Attachment to Sailing
entries.description: The call of the sea is celebrated as too strong to resist, embracing calm sailing and the crest of a raging storm. Knowledge of sailing can express belonging and practical courage. The sound rigging, a course judged patiently, and companions who know their tasks give freedom at sea its working foundation. Returning with news can give the voyage another life among those who stayed, where affection asks about more than the daring crossing. The tradition does not supply a ship, present storm, or personal seamanship.
entries.rationale: Authored attachment to sailing reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact. Source-strength clarification: Retains the explicit irresistible sea-call and calm/storm range as a public ideal, without literal personal compulsion, immunity to danger or a present sea/weather/ship/skill fact.

entries.label: Esteem for Sensual Pursuit
entries.description: Seeking intimate physical pleasure is understood as a natural and important part of life. Public attitudes can make rejection of pleasure seem difficult to comprehend. An attentive compliment and a pleasure honestly shared can give desire a language beyond possession. Admiration for pursuit can make a reserved person feel overlooked or pressured, leaving the worth of an invitation dependent on how freely the other person can answer it. That cultural valuation supplies neither a relationship nor willingness to accept a particular advance.
entries.rationale: Authored esteem for sensual pursuit reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Adoption of Prestigious Neighbor Customs
entries.description: The customs of a powerful neighboring civilization have become influential models for conduct. Borrowing from that prestige can shape public taste without eliminating local identity. An admired manner or craft can offer a household distinction borrowed from a prestigious neighbor. The learner may discover useful judgment behind the fashion, while a perfect imitation can still reveal little understanding of why the original practice mattered. The tradition alone does not identify the neighbor, establish its rule, or authorize importing a named Warcraft culture.
entries.rationale: Removes Chinese hegemony while retaining adoption under prestigious external influence. No substitute civilization is inferred from a race label. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Accepted Alchemical Metalwork
entries.description: Attempts to transform metals into gold are as culturally familiar as forging weapons. Enhancing wealth and equipment through magical craft is accepted as part of practical production. The promise of gold and the ambition for a better blade make experiment a practical investment. An impressive transformation deserves a maker's exact questions about repeatability and use, while a dazzling claim can tempt patrons to praise success before the method has earned it. The custom does not prove that an attempt succeeds or that a particular member possesses those abilities.
entries.rationale: Authored accepted alchemical metalwork reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Unadorned Practical Power
entries.description: Public grandeur and decorative display matter less than tangible strength, especially durable fortifications. A plain but effective seat of power can be admired more than a splendid ceremony. A sound wall or dependable provision gives authority something to show without a splendid costume. Practical restraint can preserve resources for what matters, while the ruler who dismisses every ornament risks overlooking the affection or memory a modest object carries. This preference does not establish a stronghold, actual poverty, or a person's chosen possessions.
entries.rationale: Retains practical austerity without importing an external ancient people or confusing indifference to display with religious asceticism. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Primacy of Defending Home
entries.description: Protecting what belongs to one's community is a foremost public value. Holding ground and safeguarding established ties can earn respect beyond the fame of conquest. The home being protected has particular people, remembered work, and relationships worth returning to. A quiet repair can serve that loyalty beside the dramatic defense, while someone invoking protection must still explain whose belonging their claim includes. The custom does not determine what is currently threatened or require an individual to accept every defensive claim.
entries.rationale: Authored primacy of defending home reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Honor in Holding the Line
entries.description: Military esteem favors remaining in place even against overwhelming opposition. Retreat can appear unacceptable despite a strong practical case for survival. The companion who remains gives others a visible promise about where they can find support. That promise can hold a force together or make a necessary withdrawal painfully hard, with those surviving the decision left to judge what the steadfastness cost. The ideal carries potential cost as well as courage, without forcing a particular fighter's decision.
entries.rationale: Authored honor in holding the line reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Defense of Inherited Identity
entries.description: Inherited customs are held to be immovable and unchangeable foundations of belonging, and people are expected to stand up for them. Proposals to alter them can be heard as threats to the community itself. A familiar gesture can carry generations of attention that a reformer sees only as inconvenience. A proposed change can therefore challenge what defenders understand as the foundation of belonging, even when the person proposing it also cares deeply about the inheritance. A particular person's disagreement remains separate from this public ideal; the tradition does not establish whether others welcome, suppress or punish it.
entries.rationale: Authored defense of inherited identity reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. This claim does not lock actual CK3 cultural evolution or settle an individual’s agreement, punishment or reception of dissent.

entries.label: Memory through Oral Telling
entries.description: A strong, persistent oral tradition passes heroes, legends and earlier lives between generations through familiar tellings. It grants neither personal memories of those events nor proof of every legend. Stories passed between generations preserve accounts of heroes, earlier lives, and shared lessons. A telling connects the present community to those who kept the account alive. A teller's pause and the detail a child asks to hear again bind an account to familiar voices. Remembering an overlooked companion can change what a celebrated deed means, while repeating an easy boast can pass an old omission to another generation. Familiarity with the tradition does not grant a personal memory of its events or authenticate every legend. Guardianship can improve education, and story exchanges can develop skills. Legends spread more readily, while schemes face reduced secrecy.
entries.rationale: Authored memory through oral telling reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.
