These are current custom opportunities or effects, not present buildings, stocks, events, offices, abilities or biographies. Building permission does not establish actual brewery presence; independently enabled routes remain separate.

entries.label: Inherited Social Rank
entries.description: Birth establishes powerful expectations about who should lead and who should serve. Proximity to authority can outweigh merit, making advancement dependent on inherited standing and access. A favored seat or a hearing granted readily can show inherited proximity to power before anyone asks about accomplishment. Those denied the same attention may understand useful work more exactly than the household admired for doing it, giving hierarchy a daily audience as well as a pedigree. The customary hierarchy does not determine the speaker's actual rank or erase an observed exception.
entries.rationale: Authored inherited social rank reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Massed Forces over Elites
entries.description: Military strength is sought through large bodies of fighters rather than concentrating resources in a few exceptional troops. Numbers and collective pressure are valued as practical advantages. The individual fighter depends on companions continuing to arrive, hold, and press together. Provision and coordination give numbers their substance; an impressive count can conceal how little a leader has done to make the many able to act as one force. The tradition does not establish an army's presence, size, or current composition.
entries.rationale: Authored massed forces over elites reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Esteem for Mercenary Service
entries.description: Soldiers are encouraged to seek paid service and reputation between their own community's wars. Working for another patron can be considered an honorable opportunity rather than automatic disloyalty. A contract can bring useful experience and a reputation worth returning with. Keeping terms gives paid service dignity, while the fighter must weigh a patron's tempting reward against obligations to companions whose trust no richer employer can simply replace. This custom establishes no current contract, employer, or military occupation.
entries.rationale: Authored esteem for mercenary service reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Recognizing Worth in Defeated Rivals
entries.description: A defeated opponent's useful ability can justify sparing them and accepting their service. Acquiring talent is valued above treating every rival as disposable. The rival's difficult shot, sound design, or useful judgment can deserve recognition even after defeat. Offering a place asks whether admiration will become an opportunity the defeated person can meaningfully take, rather than another way to spend their skill without regard for them. The ideal does not establish captivity, offered service, genuine loyalty, or a decision already made.
entries.rationale: Authored recognizing worth in defeated rivals reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Studied Military Theory
entries.description: Accumulated military writings and technical knowledge are valued resources for command. Study of strategy and the making of sound weapons and armor can matter alongside battlefield experience. A difficult campaign's lesson becomes useful when another commander can understand why it worked. Study joins the maker's reliable equipment to decisions about its use, while inherited theory must still answer a scout's report that the expected conditions have changed. The tradition does not grant a person's education or introduce a named treatise.
entries.rationale: Authored studied military theory reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Confederated Coastal Communities
entries.description: Distinct coastal and river-mouth communities can join in a confederation under a leader chosen from their rulers. Shared leadership allows cooperation while preserving considerable local difference. A common decision must leave distinct households and communities something they can defend at home. The chosen leader's standing depends on keeping local cooperation worthwhile, with shared reach gaining strength from people whose customs remain different. The tradition does not establish an active confederation or identify the speaker as an elector or chief.
entries.rationale: Removes external polity and title terminology while retaining coastal city-states, variation in scale, and selection of a common chief. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Loyalty through Honorable Service
entries.description: The bond between ruler and subordinate is esteemed when sustained through disciplined service, homage, and integrity. Respect should be strengthened by honorable deeds rather than title alone. Homage has substance through the task completed when it was difficult and the promise remembered when forgetting would be profitable. A worthy superior gives service a reason beyond fear, while an honorable subordinate can make loyalty costly by telling an unwelcome truth. This ideal does not supply a personal oath or demand agreement with every command.
entries.rationale: Preserves the source's loyalty-and-integrity concept without importing Japanese history, warrior classes, or an external code. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Competition for Courtly Favor
entries.description: Access to a ruler is a source of influence contested by eunuchs, consorts, and other members of a courtly household. Private rivalry can accompany impressive public refinement. An invitation, private hearing, or remembered introduction can make access visible without a formal appointment. Courteous attention may express affection and ambition together, while a favor's recipient learns how quickly another household can call it a debt. The familiar political pattern does not establish actual treachery, a particular household, or the speaker's motives.
entries.rationale: Authored competition for courtly favor reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Mounted Ambush Defense
entries.description: Small numbers of experienced riders and archers can answer stronger encroaching forces through raids, withdrawal, and carefully chosen ambushes. Mobility is valued as a means of resisting pressure. A carefully chosen opening lets a small force make its experience count before withdrawing from a heavier answer. Pride belongs to preserving useful riders for the next defense, with an impatient boast able to squander the knowledge that made resistance possible. The tradition does not establish a present invader or the speaker's riding and shooting skills.
entries.rationale: Authored mounted ambush defense reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Esteem for Fleeting Beauty
entries.description: Beauty gains emotional weight from the knowledge that it passes. Attentiveness to a brief moment, a changing landscape, or an accomplished work can encourage reflective appreciation rather than possession. A changing light or a work nearing its end can deserve attention precisely because it cannot be held unchanged. Sharing the moment gives pleasure another witness, while demanding that it last can turn affection for beauty into frustration with the life that makes it pass. The cultural aesthetic supplies no present object or particular feeling.
entries.rationale: Replaces the external aesthetic label with its supported impermanence, artistic appreciation, and relationship to nature. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Divine Mandate through Ritual Display
entries.rationale: Excluded because mysterious divine authority, elaborate rites, and display of divine artifacts are the defining basis of legitimacy. A generic claim of impressive rulership would erase that religious meaning.

entries.label: Civic Strongholds
entries.description: Fortified cities concentrate government and military protection, making their preservation central to public identity. Founding additional strongholds can be a source of prestige. A city's defenses protect administrative work and familiar lives as well as a ruler's standing. Founding another stronghold can offer a new center of belonging, while those celebrating its grandeur must reckon with the labor that will keep it useful. This scoped cultural account conveys the civic and defensive ideal without supplying an existing city.
entries.rationale: Retains the clearly separable military and governmental roles; the source's religious functions require independent faith context. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Prestigious Waterworks
entries.description: Constructed water features and large reservoirs receive exceptional cultural importance. Their prominence makes shaping and maintaining waterworks a recognizable communal accomplishment. A reservoir's careful form and a water feature maintained after its first display give construction a continuing audience. Such prominent works can preserve a maker's name, while their beauty and scale ask for people willing to do the less celebrated maintenance. This scoped account supplies neither a particular structure nor an active project, and makes no additional claim about their purpose.
entries.rationale: Retains the physically readable waterwork-and-reservoir component without guessing the unresolved central structure or converting it into an invented irrigation benefit. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Armed Maintenance of Internal Peace
entries.description: Protection from invasion does not remove the need for trained forces and organization. Raids, pretenders, and ambitious governors make maintaining a realm's peace a continuing political responsibility. The governor's ambition and a raider's useful opportunity can unsettle a realm whose borders appear secure. Training and organization earn their value through protecting ordinary cooperation, while the authority invoking peace must answer for how its own demands disturb it. The tradition supplies no named emperor, present rebellion, or current threat.
entries.rationale: Removes Kanmu and the borrowed terrestrial directional history while retaining the distinction between external security and internal order. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Self-Reliance and Inner Development
entries.description: A community can favor deepening its own knowledge and character over seeking foreign influence. Quiet inward improvement is valued even when distant relationships become weaker. An inherited method patiently improved can give quieter satisfaction than a distant audience's praise. Looking inward asks what the community still needs to learn about its own habits, with familiar certainty able to obstruct self-examination as readily as foreign fashion. The preference does not guarantee peace, superior wisdom, or complete isolation.
entries.rationale: Authored self-reliance and inner development reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Dynastic Appearance and Private Pleasure
entries.description: Marriage conventions remain useful for public legitimacy and household arrangements, while intimate pleasure can be accepted despite complications for pedigree. Respectable appearance and private conduct need not coincide. A polished public union can preserve household standing while private attachments follow another path. Someone expected to maintain appearances may value the arrangement or resent its demands, leaving dignity and desire in negotiations the public celebration cannot settle. The custom establishes neither a particular affair nor consent to an advance.
entries.rationale: Retains the separable social tension between pedigree, appearance, and pleasure; removes the divine justification and external identity. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Rugged Island Livelihoods
entries.description: Communities across mountainous, wooded islands are accustomed to varied rough ground and movement between difficult landscapes. Practical adaptability supports their way of life. A difficult wooded slope and the crossing to another island reward different kinds of familiar judgment. Practical knowledge can travel between neighboring communities without making their homes interchangeable, and a useful warning gives cooperation substance beyond a shared reputation for endurance. The tradition identifies no terrestrial archipelago, current location, or personal journey.
entries.rationale: Removes the Japanese archipelago and Yashima identity while retaining the actual wooded mountainous island setting as inherited familiarity. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Coexistence through Exchange
entries.description: Trade and sustained dealings with outsiders support a cosmopolitan social life in which communities of different beliefs can live alongside one another. Familiarity can make coexistence easier without settling their disagreements. A dependable trade and an ordinary meal can give unfamiliar neighbors reasons to keep dealing with one another. Repeated attention builds knowledge of the person behind the difference, while prosperity alone cannot settle which disagreements each household is willing to leave open. Shared exchange does not imply agreement in belief or universal tolerance.
entries.rationale: Retains the separable trade-supported coexistence component; borrowed worship and theological blending are not emitted in the cultural description. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Rice-Centered Agriculture
entries.description: Rice cultivation is a valued foundation of livelihood. Skilled labor can support prosperity and provisioning where suitable land allows the crop to thrive. A sound method attends to the ground and work the crop actually needs. An abundant yield gives cultivators an audience beyond their own households, while prestige belongs to the knowledge and patience behind provision as well as to the visible harvest. Cultural confidence in the craft does not establish current rice fields, an actual harvest, or superiority in every environment.
entries.rationale: Retains the exact crop and suitable-land condition without importing a terrestrial people or replacing rice with an unsupported fantasy staple. entries.label: Armed Devotional Communities
entries.rationale: Excluded because the defense of a religious community by devoted practitioners defines the practice. A generic martial description would remove its religious purpose and distinct vocation.

entries.label: Public Assemblies for Judgment
entries.description: Peers gather under an acknowledged interpreter of customary rules to settle disputes and make collective decisions. Shared judgment offers authority where distant central control is impractical. A grievance must acquire words other households can weigh against remembered custom. The respected interpreter earns attention by explaining the rule's consequence, while a strong claimant still needs the peers' acknowledgment to turn a desired answer into common judgment. The tradition does not establish a current assembly, a legal verdict, or participation by the speaker.
entries.rationale: Removes Scandinavian geography and the borrowed institution's name while retaining peer assembly and the lawspeaker function. entries.label: Remembered Shared Kinship
entries.description: Family and community bonds are emphasized as reasons to remain united. Remembering common heritage can make cooperation an obligation of belonging rather than merely temporary convenience. A shared story and the companion remembered after departure give ancestry a living audience. Remaining together asks people to make cooperation bearable through disagreement, with care for an overlooked relative testing unity more closely than another proud account of common origins. The ideal does not prove literal kinship between all members or agreement about every decision.
entries.rationale: Authored remembered shared kinship reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Inherited Upland Defense
entries.description: Knowledge passed down about wooded uplands supports defense through mobile fighting and familiarity with difficult ground. Protecting the homeland gives those skills a collective purpose. A familiar wooded approach can let a smaller force answer pressure without meeting it on the invader's terms. Passing that knowledge onward makes defensive skill an inheritance, while a new threat asks whether the old route still serves the people it once protected. The tradition supplies no present raid, savanna, or personally known battlefield.
entries.rationale: Retains inherited upland defense while removing the localized current raider threat and mandatory savanna setting. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Customary Avoidance of Animal Flesh
entries.description: Eating animal flesh is strongly disfavored, and plant-based meals are the established communal pattern. That expectation can make dietary choices socially meaningful. Careful preparation can give a plant-based meal pride and fellowship rather than make it merely an absence of meat. A host's attention to guests can show how the customary table is shared, while an individual's different needs remain a question to hear rather than a fact the custom settles. It neither identifies the food presently served nor substitutes for an individual's actual diet or bodily needs.
entries.rationale: Authored customary avoidance of animal flesh reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Martial Strength as Highest Esteem
entries.description: Fighting ability and strength receive the greatest public admiration. Children are brought up knowing how to fight and discouraged from scholarly pursuits, while weakness meets public intolerance. A formidable deed receives an audience a thoughtful argument may struggle to find. A child wanting recognition can feel the hierarchy of praise early, while the defender who remembers whom strength serves can honor necessary care despite a community inclined to celebrate only the fighter. These are demanding community values, not proof of every member's training or contempt for a vulnerable person.
entries.rationale: Authored martial strength as highest esteem reading of the fingerprinted definition. entries.label: Theological Study with Armed Duty
entries.rationale: Excluded because pursuing theology entails defending the belief community by force. Translating it into general discipline would sever its explicit religious condition.

entries.label: Service through Demonstrated Ability
entries.description: Demonstrated fighting ability is considered sufficient reason to allow service, despite barriers others would impose because of identity or standing. Proving capability matters more than a predetermined social category. The person dismissed before the test asks that the result be heard before the old category. Recognition can broaden the community's idea of a capable fighter, while unequal opportunity to train can still make the supposedly open standard difficult to reach. This principle does not give everyone the same training or guarantee an observed appointment.
entries.rationale: Authored service through demonstrated ability reading of the fingerprinted definition. entries.label: Dry-Country Warfare
entries.description: Military methods are adapted to very dry conditions. Familiarity with that environment can make a force effective where others are less prepared. Water, timing, and what a force can carry give a confident plan its actual reach. Experienced judgment knows when an apparently swift advance will leave companions unable to continue, making careful provision a military achievement beside boldness. The tradition does not locate the current encounter in arid country or establish a present campaign.
entries.rationale: Authored dry-country warfare reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Marriage as a Public Occasion
entries.description: Marriage is expected to receive conspicuous communal recognition through formal customary celebration. The union has a public place as well as an intimate one. The gathering lets households acknowledge a union and remember the care invested in its welcome. Public magnificence can give the partners delight or burden them with competing expectations, leaving the intimate promise something the guests can witness without owning it. This cultural expectation supplies no current wedding, prescribed rite, or evidence that a particular person is married.
entries.rationale: Authored marriage as a public occasion reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Esteem for Social Courtesy
entries.description: Social etiquette is valued above all else, and accomplished diplomacy receives strong public esteem. Social etiquette is valued above all else, with accomplished diplomacy receiving strong public esteem. The ability to make an exchange proceed gracefully can be admired as a meaningful skill. A thoughtful greeting notices the listener's place, an overlooked accomplishment, or the difficulty everyone else ignored. Grace gives another person room to speak without humiliation, and a diplomat's best praise can be an exchange that leaves both sides able to continue it. Esteem for etiquette does not make everyone charming or establish the correct formalities of an unobserved institution. Children more often develop Charming, and diplomacy-focused education can improve. Personal schemes can gain effectiveness, while hostile schemes against members also gain an advantage. Travel safety and court-grandeur growth can improve.

entries.label: Practical Wetland Knowledge
entries.description: Living with marshes and bogs requires familiarity with damp conditions and useful materials such as peat. Working that difficult environment is an established practical accomplishment. A sound footing and the patient handling of useful peat give damp country a practical meaning beyond discomfort. The familiar worker notices where a visitor's easy approach will fail, with good judgment making a difficult place dependable for those who know it. The custom supplies no current rain, flooded place, or personal immunity to discomfort.

entries.label: Military Life in Severe Cold
entries.description: Military practice accommodates bitter cold and harsh winds as familiar demands rather than exceptional surprises. Endurance and practical adaptation are esteemed. Preparing protection and provision before the wind worsens can spare companions a brave but needless ordeal. An experienced warning deserves attention when an impatient fighter mistakes familiar caution for fear; endurance includes preserving strength for what still has to be done. The tradition does not establish winter at the meeting place or make the speaker immune to cold.
entries.rationale: Authored military life in severe cold reading of the fingerprinted definition. entries.label: Curiosity toward Other Peoples
entries.description: Embracing everyone and fascination with all cultures are public ideals, with cultural difference inviting interest rather than automatic rejection. Learning about another people's habits can be welcomed for its own sake. An unfamiliar greeting or method can offer pleasure before it offers advantage. Curiosity earns a deeper answer when it lets the other person explain what matters, while enthusiasm can become careless if it turns someone else's inheritance into a novelty to collect. This shared openness does not guarantee personal trust, erase political conflict, or establish which foreign customs have been adopted.
entries.rationale: Authored curiosity toward other peoples reading of the fingerprinted definition. entries.label: Zandalari Monumental Urban Craft
entries.description: Zandalari urban craft joins monumental construction, intricate carving, and expressive murals to the surrounding landscape. Markets and ports connect specialized districts with distant exchange. Terraces, worked stone, and carved accounts make grandeur something generations can interpret anew. A visitor moving between monumental precincts and places of exchange encounters a civic confidence large enough to welcome distant news, while a splendid image can still leave a living tradition unrepresented. The adopted architectural tradition supplies civic identity without establishing a particular city's condition or an individual's loyalties.
entries.rationale: Zandalari identity is intrinsic to this mod-specific concept. Retains its separable architecture, civic organization, and commerce; loa reverence and active ceremonies are not assigned through the cultural entry. entries.label: Collective Devotional Commitment
entries.rationale: Excluded because strong shared religious commitment is the entire social meaning. Do not turn a cultural tradition into the individual's canonical Zealous trait or use it to alter per-character faith emphasis.

entries.label: Adaptable Practice, Enduring Belief
entries.description: The faith distinguishes its enduring convictions from restrictions that can be adjusted to changing circumstances. Revising a law or practice can preserve the faith's purpose instead of betraying it, provided the central beliefs remain intact. A changed observance can keep an old obligation meaningful when circumstances no longer fit its earlier form. Elders and reformers may disagree about where continuity ends, making the difficult question what the practice preserves rather than whether it merely looks familiar. Adaptation is conditional on that continuity, not permission to abandon the teaching.
entries.rationale: Authored adaptable practice, enduring belief reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Reciprocity with Dangerous Spirits
entries.description: Spirits are understood as beings capable of helping or harming the living. Honoring them seeks favorable treatment for the community and hostility toward its foes. Favor must be tended among powers whose intentions cannot be reduced to the living person's wishes. The same relationship can answer hope for a child's safety and fear of an enemy, with a neglected obligation giving reassurance a dangerous edge. Reverence therefore contains practical hope and caution as well as affection; it does not establish a particular spirit's presence or an individual's power to command it.
entries.rationale: Authored reciprocity with dangerous spirits reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Critical Theological Inquiry
entries.description: Questioning established interpretations and thinking critically about belief are honored forms of religious learning. A difficult question can continue a respected intellectual tradition rather than reveal disloyalty. A revered explanation gains substance when it survives an attentive challenge. The scholar who hears a pupil's inconvenient question can preserve a teaching more faithfully than one who demands repetition, while the pupil still owes the argument care rather than mere audacity. The tenet values scholarship without supplying an external school, a historical destruction, or the person's education.
entries.rationale: The readable description is resolved from the exported rules.meanings entry; removes Alexandria while retaining critical theological inquiry and challenge to the status quo. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Continuing Relationship with Ancestors
entries.description: The departed are believed to remain attentive to the living, offering guidance from beyond death. Respect and honor sustain that continuing relationship, making ancestry an obligation of care as well as a source of belonging. The honored dead remain particular people: a remembered voice, an unfinished affection, or a counsel that made an earlier choice difficult. Care can give that relationship a tangible form, while an interpreter's confidence does not relieve the living of deciding how to answer it. This teaching does not establish an actual apparition, a known ancestor's wishes, or a personal conversation with the dead.
entries.rationale: Authored continuing relationship with ancestors reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Worship without Sacred Images
entries.description: Representations of the divine are regarded as distractions that can replace understanding with attachment to an object. Removing such images from places of worship is understood as protecting the faithful from that error. A cherished image can comfort the faithful and become the thing they protect instead of the meaning it was meant to disclose. Refusing that substitution gives plain worship its seriousness, while removing an admired object can cost something even to someone who accepts the reason. The teaching does not prohibit every form of ordinary art or establish an image currently present.
entries.rationale: Authored worship without sacred images reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Direct Personal Access to the Sacred
entries.description: No person or priestly class is considered qualified to speak for the divine on another person's behalf. The search for sacred understanding is personal and accessible without imposed clerical mediation. Advice can be useful without giving its keeper ownership of another person's conscience. Companions may share a difficult question, but a persuasive teacher still has to earn agreement rather than claim that office alone settles what the sacred asks. Freedom and fellowship can accompany strong conviction; rejection of priestly authority is not necessarily rejection of the sacred itself.
entries.rationale: Authored direct personal access to the sacred reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Protection of Sacred Journeys
entries.description: Journeys to holy places deserve protection from those who would harm their participants. Taking up arms for that protection can be understood as an obligation of faith rather than merely military ambition. The vulnerable traveler gives martial service a purpose more particular than a magnificent victory. A guarded road can let others approach what they revere, while the protector must reckon with the difference between keeping that journey possible and using its holiness to justify any expedition. The tenet does not establish a pilgrimage underway, a present attacker, or a duty for every member to become a guard.

entries.label: Simplicity for Spiritual Clarity
entries.description: The faith teaches that material pursuit obscures divine truth and that enlightenment requires a life devoted to simplicity without luxury. Giving up a splendid possession can release attention that its care once consumed. The austere choice deserves meaning through what it makes possible, while admiration for one's own restraint can become another appetite that the simpler life has failed to quiet. The principle concerns the faith's ideal, not proof that a particular believer is poor, a recluse, or unable to enjoy anything. Secluded meditation offers possible relief and theological insight. Eligible county or duchy rulers with at most three domain holdings may choose landless adventure, subject to actual eligibility.
entries.rationale: Authored simplicity for spiritual clarity reading of the fingerprinted definition. entries.label: Reading Divine Meaning in the Sky
entries.description: The night sky is regarded as a visible field of divine meaning, whose patterns may disclose truths about the world. Learning to interpret those patterns is esteemed as a serious pursuit. A patient observer seeks relations a hurried glance would miss, with awe and careful inquiry sharing the same sky. Rival readings can make a forecast a question of judgment as well as devotion, leaving wonder meaningful without turning uncertainty into a guaranteed answer. This conviction supplies no observed omen, prescribed calendar, certain prediction, or personal ability to read one.

entries.label: Moral Responsibility of Rulers
entries.description: Governing carries an obligation to encourage what the faith considers good and resist what it condemns. Authority is justified through moral responsibility rather than power alone. A ruler's finest praise is care that reaches beyond a flattering audience. Hearing the petition that costs a favored household something can give moral authority substance, while a public defense of righteousness must remain answerable to those living under the decision. The standard does not settle every disputed judgment or establish that an actual ruler has fulfilled it.
entries.rationale: Authored moral responsibility of rulers reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Devotion to a Divine Aspect
entries.description: Mortals are understood to fall short of the divine in its fullness. Choosing one aspect to worship, emulate, and serve offers a meaningful path toward it. A chosen aspect gives emulation something particular to attend to: a quality admired, a duty practiced, a familiar example before a difficult choice. Another devotee's different focus can show the limits of one's own path without making its attention meaningless. Focused devotion need not claim complete understanding or make every believer devoted to the same aspect.
entries.rationale: Retains single-aspect emulation without importing a real-world pantheon, avatar, or named devotional tradition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Blood Offering and Shared Flesh
entries.description: Sacrificing sentient life is regarded as the most valuable offering. Blood is given to the divine, while consuming the deceased's flesh is believed to convey wisdom and strength. An offering's terrible cost can become part of the favor the faithful hope to receive. Sharing the flesh joins the sacred claim to an intimate act of consumption, with reverence and the desire for another's strength able to occupy the same expectation. The tenet joins offering and consumption without proving a supernatural transfer or establishing a current victim, meal, or act of participation.
entries.rationale: Authored blood offering and shared flesh reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact. Source-strength clarification: Restores the explicit highest valuation of sentient sacrifice rather than weakening it to an especially valuable option. Religious valuation and claimed transfer remain distinct from actual participation, a victim, consent or successful supernatural gain.

entries.label: Sacred Esteem for Sexual Pleasure
entries.description: Sexual pleasure is valued as an experience that draws mortals closer to the divine. Seeking and honoring desire can be interpreted as religious fulfillment rather than shame. Tenderness and desire can give devotion a close, embodied language. A pleasure freely shared can be honored with gratitude, while someone using sacred praise to pressure another reveals a difference between celebrating desire and deciding another person's wishes for them. Approval of pleasure does not establish another person's consent, a particular relationship, or a believer's willingness to participate.
entries.rationale: Authored sacred esteem for sexual pleasure reading of the fingerprinted definition. entries.label: Belief and Cultural Belonging
entries.description: The community understands its faith and culture as closely joined. Shared belonging strengthens mutual ties but can make outsiders less readily accepted, even when an outsider respects the teaching. A familiar greeting or household observance can signal belonging before a creed is discussed. Shared recognition gives companionship warmth, while a sincere newcomer can discover how much acceptance depends on inherited habits they have not yet learned. The tenet does not collapse a person's actual culture and faith into one identity or establish universal hostility.
entries.rationale: Resolves the missing top-level description from the complete exported meaning; preserves both solidarity and foreigner exclusion without selecting a named people. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Shared Resources as a Sacred Right
entries.description: The divine is understood to intend an equal share of the world's resources for everyone. Holding wealth in common and redistributing what the powerful have appropriated are treated as obligations of justice. A full store beside a hungry household can become an accusation about how divine intention has been neglected. Redistribution asks the powerful to surrender an advantage, while common care still has to decide how labor, need, and useful stewardship will be acknowledged. The teaching does not establish the community's actual property arrangements or authorize inventing a completed redistribution.
entries.rationale: Authored shared resources as a sacred right reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Ritual Participation as Belonging
entries.description: Communal rites are believed to invoke the divine's actual presence rather than merely represent it. Joining those practices is treated as a defining mark of true belief, and refusal or inability to participate can carry exclusion. The gathering is understood as meeting sacred presence together, giving participation a weight that private sincerity alone may not satisfy. An absent companion can therefore provoke concern, suspicion, or exclusion, with the community's judgment able to wound someone who still believes. This claim supplies no particular rite, sacramental object, or proven divine manifestation.
entries.rationale: Retains the demanding participation criterion without importing bread, wine, a church institution, or another real-world sacrament. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Final Cleansing and Chosen Death
entries.description: For the old or sick, a final cleansing rite is understood to remove sin before a deliberate death prevents its return. The practice is valued as a religious ending to life rather than simply ordinary medical care. The promised final purity gives death a meaning the faithful may find consoling and the living family difficult to bear. Someone contemplating the rite can weigh release against unfinished affections, while reverence for the practice cannot settle another person's choice or suffering for them. This teaching establishes no person's illness, consent, approaching death, or present rite.
entries.rationale: Preserves the source's explicit age-or-illness context and intentional death without importing a named historical sect or claiming a rite occurs. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Religious Approval of Consumption
entries.description: Consumption is held to be good in itself, with acquiring and using more goods praised for expanding cities and advancing society. Acquiring and using more goods can be treated as an expression of progress rather than a distraction from belief. A thriving exchange and goods put into use can appear signs of society moving forward. Religious esteem gives acquisition an audience beyond private pleasure, while a believer can ask whether a dazzling purchase actually advances life or merely advertises its owner's appetite. This valuation does not establish prosperity, personal greed, or a particular purchase.
entries.rationale: Authored religious approval of consumption reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact. Source-strength clarification: Restores the effective tenet's absolute-good claim as good in itself, preserving city growth and social advance. Personal questioning neither weakens the public ideal nor establishes its reception.

entries.label: Spiritual Power in Taken Heads
entries.description: The head is believed to contain its owner's essential spiritual substance. Taking it and extracting its contents are understood as ways to claim that power. A preserved head can represent an enduring claim upon someone whose life has ended. The sacred purpose lies in the substance believed recoverable from it, making the trophy more intimate than an emblem of victory and more disturbing than an ordinary keepsake. The teaching gives trophies a religious purpose beyond display, without establishing a victim, a held trophy, or an actual gain in power.
entries.rationale: Authored spiritual power in taken heads reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Sanctity of Earth and Heights
entries.description: The earth's depths, stony defenses, hidden paths, and high summits are regarded as privileged ways to approach the divine. Shelter and pilgrimage can share reverence for the land's substance. A narrow passage, enduring stone, or arduous approach can give sacred shelter a form the faithful can imagine closely. Reverence attends to what protects and what must be traversed, joining the security of a redoubt to the seriousness of seeking beyond ordinary comfort. The tenet does not establish an underground dwelling, a mountain location, or a journey in progress.
entries.rationale: Preserves the source's combination of roots, stone, hidden trails, and summits instead of narrowing the concept to underground worship alone. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Strength as Approach to Divinity
entries.description: Increasing one's strength is treated as movement toward the divine. Unceasing struggle and daily growth in strength are sacred demands of a worthwhile life. A difficult exercise or a resolve maintained through discouragement gives improvement something to answer for. Sacred esteem can recognize discipline as well as force, while a boast of greatness leaves the harder question of whether the devotee can still learn. The teaching does not decide whether every kind of strength is bodily or establish the believer's abilities, victory, or appetite for a current fight.
entries.rationale: Authored strength as approach to divinity reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact. Source-strength clarification: Restores the effective tenet's unceasing struggle and daily growth in strength toward divinity. This is an ongoing sacred demand, not proof of a follower's bodily ability, present battle or compulsory individual action.

entries.label: Openness to Death Traditions
entries.description: The faith recognizes that traditions centered on Death can contain worthwhile knowledge. Their followers need not be condemned merely for belonging to another tradition. Another tradition's account of mourning, remembered obligation, or a worthy ending can invite attention rather than immediate condemnation. A believer can learn from its care for the dead while still questioning its explanation of what lies beyond them. This openness does not establish conversion, doctrinal agreement, undead status, or personal command of death magic.
entries.rationale: Authored openness to death traditions reading of the fingerprinted definition. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. entries.label: Nonviolence through Cosmic Kinship
entries.description: All beings are understood as participants in one cosmic order. Violence against another therefore injures the whole to which the aggressor also belongs. The supposed enemy remains part of the relationship that makes one's own life possible. A moment of restraint can acknowledge that shared place even when anger feels justified, leaving nonviolence a demanding consequence of kinship rather than mere indifference to injury. Refusing harm is a consequence of that shared relationship, without proving cosmic events or granting the believer knowledge of every being's nature.
entries.rationale: Removes the real-world doctrinal label while preserving the source's interconnectedness-based rejection of violence. Portable flavor revision: the added concrete examples are possible expressions of this adopted concept, not an enacted scene, role, possession, personal biography or additional contributor. Original semantic qualifications remain intact.

entries.label: Openness to Disorder Traditions
entries.description: Traditions concerned with Disorder or Fel are considered possible sources of worthwhile understanding. Their followers are not automatically condemned simply for differing in belief. An unsettling account of change can deserve a hearing without earning permission for every practice defended in its name. Curiosity gives disagreement room to become understanding, while the believer still has to judge what another path asks them to accept. That qualified openness does not establish approval of every practice, demonic identity, or the believer's ability to wield fel power.

entries.label: Close-Kin Marriage as Sacred Emulation
entries.description: Marriage between close relatives is understood to imitate the sacred unions of creation's earliest beings. The faith teaches that such unions preserve valued qualities and seek divine favor against evil. A union can be praised for preserving a sacred lineage before the partners' own wishes are heard. Emulation lends family continuity immense prestige, while disagreement within the household can expose how differently devotion, affection, and obligation understand the same proposed bond. This is a lineage teaching, not proof of biological benefit or a particular marriage.

entries.label: Shared Moral Conclave
entries.description: Participating traditions are recognized as sharing moral concerns despite differences in sacred explanation. Other recognized branches are judged wayward rather than irredeemable enemies; birthplace alone establishes no such affiliation. Care and resistance to cruelty can give cooperation substance without requiring common worship or erasing disagreement. Conferring titles can bring relief, without prescribing an individual gift or making every believer generous. entries.label: Openness to Elemental Traditions
entries.description: Religious traditions centered on the elements are recognized as having knowledge worth considering. Difference in worship does not by itself make their followers evil. Another path's attention to enduring earth, moving water, or a formidable flame can offer language for questions the believer already has. Recognizing that understanding gives an unfamiliar devotee a hearing without requiring identical patrons or every rite to be shared. entries.label: Inquiry into Divine Mystery
entries.description: The limits of mortal understanding make divine mysteries reasons to seek knowledge rather than excuses to remain ignorant. Attentive investigation of the world can be an act of religious seriousness. A surprising ordinary detail can reward the attention another person dismissed as unnecessary. Wonder asks for investigation rather than an easy claim of certainty, with an admired teacher's explanation remaining open to the question that reveals how much is still unknown. The tenet does not identify a secret teaching, initiate every believer, or grant occult ability.

entries.label: Pain as Blessing
entries.description: Pain is taught as the universal emotion and violence as the universal language. Inflicting pain is understood as bestowing a blessing, while receiving it is treated as receiving grace. The faithful can hear an inflicted wound as a gift even where its recipient hears cruelty. That conviction makes suffering intimate and consequential, while a declaration of blessing can conceal a profound disagreement over what the other person wanted or what grace means. Sacred approval of violence does not establish a victim's consent, an individual's desire, or a present violent act.

entries.label: Violent Rejection of Corrupted Piety
entries.description: The faith portrays a degraded religious order as sheltering enemies behind an appearance of piety. Killing followers of rival faiths within that religious tradition and destroying artifacts can be praised as steps toward liberation. An old title or treasured artifact can be treated as evidence of the very corruption it once promised to oppose. The hoped-for liberation gives destruction a purpose, while enemies described through sacred accusation remain people whose actual nature the accusation does not prove. Hope for a coming savior accompanies this rejection; the teaching does not prove that targeted people are demons.

entries.label: Hidden Belief under Mortal Threat
entries.description: When a person's life is threatened, outward profession of another faith is permitted if their true belief remains inwardly intact. Preserving life does not require genuine conversion under that condition. A hostile listener may receive the words demanded without receiving the speaker's allegiance. A prayer kept inwardly meaningful or a conviction privately remembered can preserve continuity through the threat, with survival and faithfulness understood as compatible under this narrow permission. The permission does not extend to ordinary convenience, profit, social embarrassment, or abandoning the retained conviction.

entries.label: Sacred Obligations toward Elders
entries.description: Respectful service to parents and obedience to elders are treated as foundations of moral goodness. After parents die, appropriate burial and worship sustain those obligations. Listening when counsel is inconvenient, giving care when dependence costs something, and remembering the departed make obedience a continuing relationship. The elder's standing asks more than public compliments, while the family must still decide how inherited duty serves those living now. The teaching does not establish a particular parent's wishes, a prescribed ceremony, or a believer's actual family relationships.

entries.label: Infiltration as Devotional Sacrifice
entries.description: When ordinary warfare cannot serve the cause, infiltration and deception against its enemies are regarded as religious duties. Willingness to face pain and give one's life is praised as commitment to a greater purpose. The concealed purpose gives a convincing appearance sacred seriousness. A devotee's willingness to endure for the cause can earn admiration, while the life risked remains tied to people and affections that a magnificent account of sacrifice can too readily overlook. entries.label: Celebration through Blood Offering
entries.description: Life is understood as depending on blood drawn from animals, kin, and enemies. The divine is therefore considered owed a share through communal offerings. The celebration joins dependence on living blood to a public acknowledgment of what the gods are owed. Company can give the offering exuberance and belonging, while a participant who recoils faces the hard difference between communal joy and the cost that sustains it. The teaching gives bloody celebration a rationale, but the teaching establishes neither a current victim nor a festival occurring now.

entries.label: Sacred Order through Balanced Rule
entries.description: Individuals, the natural world, and society are expected to be brought into balance. A legitimate sacred ruler is understood to guide that common order, with the community following its direction. A decision is judged through the relations it keeps workable among people, their world, and the authority directing them. The promise of balance can justify patient adjustment or command obedience, making the ruler's claimed harmony answerable to those asked to live within it. The tenet does not identify an actual ruler, prove divine appointment, or guarantee agreement about what harmony requires.

entries.label: Enjoyment as Gratitude to Creation
entries.description: The world's pleasures are understood as gifts of the divine. Taking joy in them honors creation, while refusing its bounty is regarded as snubbing the work of creation. A fine meal, beautiful work, or pleasure shared with a companion can become an answer of gratitude. Delight has spiritual worth, while the devotee's attention is tested when insisting on enjoyment begins to overlook another person's need or pain. This religious valuation does not establish personal indulgence, available luxuries, or willingness to accept every offered pleasure.

entries.label: Sacred Duty to Resist Darkness
entries.description: Prayer alone is considered insufficient: the faith calls for determined struggle against what it regards as darkness. Courage and willingness to fight or die are praised, while fear is condemned within that ideal. The beloved life being defended gives courage an object beyond the prestige of a fearless name. A companion's sacrifice can deserve honor while remaining a loss someone mourns, and the believer who still feels fear must face a teaching that condemns it. entries.label: Sacrifice of Persons
entries.description: Offering a person's life through killing is regarded as the most valuable sacrifice and foremost proof of devotion. Praising that surrender gives the sacred claim precedence at terrible cost, with hopes of religious worth unable to make the death merely symbolic. entries.label: Understanding through Self-Discovery
entries.description: Understanding the world is believed to require understanding oneself. A long and difficult inward journey can be valued as serious religious work rather than withdrawal from all responsibility. The wish to be right can direct a person who believes they are calmly examining the world. entries.description: Law is regarded as the work of generations of devout judgment. Following it is itself an act of piety, and no wrongdoer's position should place them above its authority. The powerful defendant and the favored household should answer the same inherited standard, while a faithful judge must reckon with the people whose lives make the rule's consequences particular. entries.label: Openness to Life Traditions

entries.label: Worship among Stones and Open Air
entries.description: Constructed temples are regarded as distractions from the divine creation surrounding the faithful. Arranging natural stones beneath the open sky is valued as a fitting way to approach the creator. The stone's weight, weathered surface, and relation to the open world give the sacred approach a plain grandeur. A worked circle can direct attention to creation rather than enclosure, with care for its form still tested by whether the arrangement helps understanding or becomes another distraction. entries.label: Lunar Shelter and Ancestral Reunion
entries.description: The stars are believed to watch over the faithful, while moonlight offers comfort and healing through hardship. Hope of rejoining ancestors in the firmament gives celestial reverence a relationship to death as well as present care. entries.label: Sacred Encounter among High Peaks

Distance and height can give an ascent religious meaning. The imagined ascent gives reverence effort, distance, and a change of perspective. Leaving cultivated familiarity can make attention more serious, while the hardship admired by one pilgrim remains something another person's needs may prevent them from bearing. entries.label: Spiritual Calling from Birth
entries.description: Birth is understood to carry a destiny, with some people believed especially marked for extraordinary spiritual leadership and magical gifts. Such a calling can attract reverence and expectation before accomplishment. Expectation can give a child's life an audience before any accomplishment earns it. A praised destiny brings hope and pressure, leaving the person believed chosen to discover whether others will hear the future they themselves want to seek. The teaching does not prove that a particular person was chosen or grant any actual magical ability.

entries.label: Sacred Life beyond Civilization
entries.description: Civilization is regarded as an unnatural attempt to force imposed order onto creation. Wild, unencumbered life and naturism are praised as closer to divine intention. Freedom from accumulated possessions can promise a closer relationship with the world as given. The admirer of unencumbered life must still consider what shelter and care let vulnerable companions remain part of it, rather than praise hardship only another person bears. entries.label: Cultivated Effortless Awareness
entries.description: Through sustained artistic, craft, or martial practice, the ideal is for the body to answer all challenges without deliberate thought, in an immediate, attentive response. The ideal is cultivated awareness expressed through the body, not loss of mind or will. A practiced hand can answer before a rehearsed explanation catches up, giving craft or movement an attentive immediacy. The ideal values awareness made dependable through repetition, with an elegant performance carrying work the watching audience may never see. The tenet supplies no training history or an individual's mastery.

entries.label: Openness to Order Traditions
entries.description: Traditions centered on Order or the Arcane are regarded as possible sources of worthwhile learning. Difference in worship alone does not make their followers evil. Another tradition's account of relation, pattern, and disciplined understanding can deserve attention without becoming the believer's whole explanation. A useful insight may survive disagreement about its source, while the listener retains judgment over the practices offered alongside it. entries.label: Peace through Avoiding Violence
entries.description: Violence is condemned for the suffering, pain, and regret it produces. Avoiding it whenever possible is understood to build a more secure community for the faithful. A patient answer can preserve a relationship anger would otherwise destroy. The ideal asks what lets people return unharmed and keep a community workable, while sincere aversion to violence still has to face the difficult choices that make avoidance costly. The principle retains that practical qualification without inventing an additional blanket permission for aggression.

entries.label: Privacy of Religious Practice
entries.description: The community seeks to be left free to follow its own practices and regards outsiders' beliefs as likewise their own business. Separation can protect a valued way of life without a wish to govern other people's worship. A household's quiet observance deserves room without making every neighbor adopt it. Keeping others' beliefs their own business can sustain a practical peace, while an outsider's demand for public proof tests how securely that freedom is understood. entries.label: Holy Places as Seats of Authority

The organization of worship and the location of power are closely joined. A revered destination also gives decisions a recognized place from which to reach the faithful. Pilgrimage and authority can reinforce one another, while distance from the sacred seat raises questions about whose counsel can be heard and whose needs its leaders understand. entries.label: Affection without Exclusive Possession
entries.description: Love is expected to resemble the divine's unconditional care rather than ownership of another person's affections. Exclusive claims can therefore be challenged as restrictions on generous attachment. Affection gains worth through being offered rather than held as another person's exclusive possession. Generosity asks for attention to actual wishes and responsibilities, with the refusal to claim ownership unable by itself to settle jealousy or another partner's boundaries. entries.label: Sacred Worth of Building and Care
entries.description: Constructing something, protecting it, and helping it flourish are regarded as sources of virtue. Transformation can belong to care rather than be condemned simply because it changes what existed. A repaired shelter, a craft passed onward, or a living work allowed to grow gives care a tangible achievement. A changed form can keep the relationship meaningful, while demanding an unchanged possession can frustrate the flourishing that first made it worth protecting. Improving what a society can accomplish can itself carry religious significance. An invention that makes difficult work possible gives improvement a grateful audience. Religious praise can delight the maker and burden them with grand expectations, while a discovery's worth still has to answer the people living with its consequences. This valuation supplies no device, discovery, or scientific occupation for a particular believer.

entries.label: Devotion amid an Age of Decline
entries.description: The world is understood to be in an age of degraded teaching. Wealth, scholarship, and exalted birth offer no sufficient refuge; faithful adherence to the true precepts is held to open the way to rebirth in a blessed realm beyond that decline. An ordinary person's faithful attention can carry hope that rank and impressive learning cannot purchase. Devotion gives an age described as decline a way forward, while the promise of another realm leaves the believer choosing how to care for those still living here. The teaching neither proves that realm's existence nor guarantees any person's fate.

entries.label: Purification through Religious Pursuit
entries.description: Actively pursuing those judged impious is treated as proof of devotion. Interrogation is understood to seek repentance or expose an enemy, and persistent resistance is taken as evidence of irredeemable impiety. A refusal to confess can be read as proof that questioning must continue, making the accused person's resistance part of the accusation. Zeal gives coercion a claim to holy purpose, while certainty about the judgment need not tell the interrogator what is actually true. entries.label: Hierarchy of Religious Understanding
entries.description: Those believed to possess understanding from birth receive the highest esteem, followed by those who willingly seek it. Those who lack understanding and do not seek to learn are assigned the lowest standing. A willing pupil can earn standing through the attention an admired natural talent takes for granted. Ranking people by understanding gives learning immense value, while those enforcing the hierarchy must decide whether an unfamiliar question reveals ignorance or insight they have yet to recognize. entries.label: Power as the Measure of Right
entries.description: The faith understands judgments of righteousness as changing with those who command power. Pursuing power itself is therefore praised as the only truly righteous cause. A patron's success can change which argument receives a hearing, leaving yesterday's praised rule vulnerable to today's stronger will. The sacred ambition can make dependence a painful contradiction: someone seeking command may acquire it through obedience they hoped to escape. This severe worldview supplies no actual authority, successful scheme, or automatic ambition to an individual believer.

entries.label: Life through Repeated Birth
entries.description: Death is believed to open another life within a succession of births. Present existence is understood as one part of a longer continuity. An unfinished affection or a life's unfulfilled work can acquire hope beyond one ending. The departed remain missed in the present even where another birth is trusted, and the promise of continuity does not tell a grieving household whom it should expect to meet again. The teaching does not give the speaker memories of earlier lives, establish a specific reincarnation, or identify who they will become.

entries.label: Theology in Public Judgment
entries.description: Religious judgment is considered relevant to settling worldly disputes. Spiritual qualities can inform decisions ordinarily treated as legal or political, making the boundary between those kinds of argument thin. A dispute over land or obligation can become an argument about what a worthy life owes the sacred. The learned judgment gains public consequence, while the person losing the case can question whether religious insight or a favored household's advantage actually directed it. The tenet supplies no enacted law, existing ruling, or universally agreed measure of righteousness.

entries.label: Shared Authority with a Parent Faith
entries.description: Differences of practice are treated as less important than shared central teachings and continuing acceptance of a parent faith's ultimate authority. Distinct worship can therefore coexist with a common arbiter. A familiar observance can keep its distinctive voice while accepting a common final authority. Shared allegiance gives difference a recognized place, while a difficult ruling tests whether that room survives when the parent path asks for a change the local community resents. The tenet does not erase current doctrinal differences or supply a named religious head.

entries.label: Reverence through Consuming Flesh
entries.description: The flesh of people is regarded as bearing a sacred spark that should be honored through consumption rather than discarded through burial or burning. Consumption gives reverence an intimate form in the flesh believed worthy of more than disposal. The sacred claim can make refusal seem a failure to honor what remains, while the act retains a cost and meaning another person's appetite or consent cannot be assumed to share. The practice receives religious approval without establishing a current meal, a victim, or the believer's appetite and participation.

entries.label: Shared Joy in Worship
entries.description: Public celebration is valued as a way to honor the divine and strengthen community bonds. Worship is understood as something to rejoice in together rather than keep wholly private. Music, food, and the pleasure of familiar company can give gratitude a voice larger than a solitary prayer. A younger participant and an elder may love different parts of the same gathering, with shared rejoicing able to carry continuity without demanding identical feeling. The teaching supplies no present festival, mandatory calendar, assembled crowd, or prescribed ceremony.

entries.label: Sacred Respect for Guests
entries.description: Hospitality is regarded as one of the greatest virtues. Guests within the home, mortal or divine, are owed utmost honor and respect. The welcome gives sacred esteem an object close enough to notice: a guest's unease, a preference remembered, a place offered without humiliation. Respect is tested when receiving someone well brings inconvenience rather than an impressive favor in return. The tenet does not establish a guest's identity, an actual divine visitor, or the host's available resources.

entries.label: The Hunt as Offering
entries.description: An offering earned through one's own hunting is considered especially worthy. Following the example of ancestors gives that effort sacred meaning beyond its material result. The effort personally borne gives an offering substance beyond its price. Preparation, pursuit, and attentive handling of the yield make ancestral example a practice the devotee answers through care, with a magnificent trophy alone unable to settle how worthy the offering is. The tenet does not establish a hunt, a kill, a species of prey, or a particular believer's hunting ability.

entries.label: Prepared Birthplaces and Divine Blessing
entries.description: Bathing places used for childbirth are expected to be cleansed and prepared through appropriate rites seeking divine favor. Care for the place and hope for blessing are joined in the faith's understanding of birth. Careful preparation gives hope for a new life a place the family can attend to together. Cleanliness and sacred attention can comfort those waiting, while the blessing sought remains something revered rather than an outcome anyone's confidence can guarantee. The teaching supplies no current pregnancy, available bathhouse, exact rite, or guaranteed outcome.

entries.label: Destruction as the Beginning of Renewal
entries.description: New creation is understood to require an ending of what came before. Destruction can therefore carry sacred significance as a condition of renewal rather than appear only as loss. An ending can be defended as making room for what could not otherwise begin. The claim is hardest when someone else cherishes the work to be removed, leaving the destroyer answerable for whether promised renewal has substance beyond the pleasure of breaking it. The teaching does not establish that a particular act will produce improvement or identify anything that should presently be destroyed.

entries.label: Holiness through Successful Deception
entries.description: Successful deception is honored as a profound sacred art. Convincing others can confer esteem, while overcoming one's own resistance to a lie is portrayed as exceptional power. A convincing appearance gives the deceiver a triumph in another mind's confidence. Self-deception carries the same art inward, where the achievement can be praised even as it makes a sincerely held conviction difficult to distinguish from a successful lie. This is broad religious approval of deception, not proof that the believer lies or that self-deception grants supernatural ability.

entries.label: Willing and Punitive Life Offerings
entries.description: Voluntarily giving one's life in ceremony, and killing people judged to have committed unforgivable offenses against the gods, are regarded as ways to approach the divine. Both willingness and punitive condemnation belong to the teaching. The willing offering can be honored as a cost the devotee bears personally, while punitive killing gives a sacred accusation power over another life. Both bring the faithful toward the divine in their teaching, without making the same account of willingness apply to the condemned. It does not prove guilt, consent, a sentenced victim, or a rite underway.

entries.label: Guests within Divine Nature
entries.description: The natural world is regarded as divine creation, with people living within it as guests. Trees, animals, and the ground itself deserve respectful treatment rather than being valued only for use. A tree, an animal, and the ground sustaining another season belong to relationships people enter rather than merely materials they own. Gratitude can find delight in that abundance, while immediate advantage is weighed against lives that should continue after the actor is gone. The teaching does not independently impose vegetarianism, grant natural powers, or establish a particular sacred site.

entries.label: Openness to Shadow Traditions
entries.description: Traditions centered on Shadow are regarded as holding something worth learning despite differences of belief. Their followers are not automatically condemned for those differences. An unsettling account of concealment or inward power can be worth examining without condemning its keeper on sight. Respect gives difficult differences a hearing, while curiosity still leaves the believer free to reject the demand or danger another practice presents. The teaching does not establish devotion to the Void, acceptance of every practice, or personal access to shadow magic.
