entries.label: Good through Submission and Effort
entries.description: Goodness is understood to originate in divine will. A worthy life submits to that will and strives to put it into practice, joining obedience to active effort. A difficult duty gives obedience more substance than words of reverence alone. The believer must still decide how to recognize and carry out the divine will, leaving honest interpretation a responsibility that a confident human command cannot automatically relieve. The teaching does not identify an unprovided command, define every struggle as armed, or guarantee agreement about its interpretation.

entries.label: Reverence for the Life-Giving Sun
entries.description: The sun is honored as the enduring source of light and life and as a sovereign presence above the world. Its reliability and power give solar devotion a distinctive object. Warmth and reliable return give sovereign power something beloved as well as formidable. Gratitude can cherish the promise of another day, with the source of life an object of attention rather than a guarantee that every darkness has already passed. The tenet supplies no named sun deity, prescribed seasonal rite, or personal access to fire or Light magic.

entries.label: Reverence for Divine Bears
entries.description: Bears are believed to manifest divine beings. Their lives deserve particular respect, and killing one during a hunt requires reverent treatment rather than casual disposal. An admired bear can give divine strength a living form close enough to encounter and vulnerable enough to be harmed. A successful hunter's judgment includes what respectful treatment asks afterward, leaving the sacred regard meaningful without pretending the animal's death has no cost. The teaching does not forbid every hunt, establish a specific rite, or make an individual bear an observed god.
entries.rationale: Retains the exact bear-specific belief and respectful-hunting qualification while replacing an opaque label with its supplied meaning. entries.label: Protection Tax and Confessional Service
entries.description: Military service is reserved for the faithful, while people of other beliefs are expected to contribute a tax in return for protection. Religious membership therefore shapes distinct public obligations. A household can owe protection a contribution different from the faithful soldier's service. The distinction makes belief publicly consequential, while a ruler invoking the arrangement must answer whether those paying receive the security their obligation is meant to support. The teaching does not prove that a ruler enacted the arrangement or establish an actual payment or exemption.

entries.label: Religious Union against Existential Darkness
entries.description: The faith understands a gathering darkness as threatening the world's survival and calls for determined common resistance. Other beliefs can be acknowledged while the community insists on the superior righteousness of its own struggle and accepts extreme measures for it. A shared danger can give unfamiliar allies reasons to stand together without settling their rival claims to truth. The faith's superior-righteousness claim remains beside that recognition, making cooperation demanding when extreme means are defended as the price of everyone's survival. The teaching does not confirm a present cosmic threat or identify particular enemies.

entries.label: Commitment beyond the Odds
entries.description: Refusal to surrender the cause is praised even when success appears unlikely. Willingness to fight or die expresses the community's ideal of unbroken conviction. An uncertain cause tests commitment after magnificent promises cease to reassure. A companion's praise can sustain devotion and sharpen its cost, while the person asked to persist remains someone whose fear, affection, and doubt do not disappear because surrender is condemned. This teaching does not erase an individual's fear, provide an actual battle, or establish that every believer chooses sacrifice.

entries.label: Renunciation of Accumulated Wealth
entries.description: The faith teaches that acquiring material wealth corrupts the heart and that its acquisition must be shunned to focus on what matters spiritually. A splendid purse can distract its owner, yet the wish to be praised for an empty one can become a possession of its own. Renunciation asks what attention can serve after accumulation loses its claim. entries.label: War as Religious Belonging
entries.description: War is treated as integral to faith, and refusal to fight for the divine can be used to deny someone's standing as a true believer. Martial participation is therefore more than a permitted means of protection. A reluctant fighter can cherish the faith and still have belonging questioned for refusing its martial demand. Public recognition ties conviction to service, giving war a social cost beyond danger and making devotion something the community may judge by what the believer will risk. The teaching supplies no current war or actual judgment of the speaker's membership.

conditionalReadings.label: Patient Judgment of Stone
conditionalReadings.description: Mining is an inherited conversation with stone: the seam that promises iron, the passage whose supports deserve another look, the warning an impatient newcomer would rather ignore. Patient excavation earns standing because a mistake can bury other people's work and lives. Dwarven pride also notices beauty underground, from a mineral's unexpected gleam to the exact meeting of cut surfaces. The digger who gives up a rich find to keep companions safe can deserve more respect than the loudest prospector. Knowing what the mountain will bear matters as much as knowing what can be taken from it.

conditionalReadings.label: Mining Knowledge Worth Taking Seriously
conditionalReadings.description: A deceptive seam, a place where a foot must land, and a passage that makes a towering visitor crawl are matters of exact inherited expertise. Gold's gleam rewards patient digging before any broker names its price. An old miner's warning can sound like timidity to someone who has never heard a roof begin to move; younger diggers can resent it when recognition and a rich find seem close. The outsider who survives through that knowledge and praises the guide like an amusing pet has missed the achievement. Pride lives in bringing companions and discoveries back through the same stone.

conditionalReadings.label: Workmanship as Family Standing
conditionalReadings.description: Family workmanship puts a maker's reputation into a hinge that closes cleanly, a blade with its balance exact, or a carved figure that catches torchlight. Techniques refined across generations deserve close teaching and an equally exact audience. A compliment carries weight when it notices the difficult fitting rather than merely calling the object fine. An inherited masterpiece can preserve affection for its maker long after that maker is gone. Hiding a defect may save the family boast for a season while betraying the standard that made the work worth inheriting. Pride therefore asks for a sound work as well as a celebrated name.
conditionalReadings.guard: Inherited family craft remains central. No particular clan, heirloom, trade, personal skill, or titan faith is selected; no metalwork tradition is required.

conditionalReadings.label: Inherited Craft that Welcomes a New Idea
conditionalReadings.description: Inherited techniques become something a new mind can understand, question, and improve. Family craft prizes the elegant solution hidden in a tiny mechanism and the patient explanation that lets an apprentice see why it works. Relatives can remember an earlier failure and still share the maker's hopes; an objection from someone who understands the design need not be disloyalty. A pupil's first independent success tests the teacher who encouraged audacity but dislikes being surpassed. The finest inheritance can be a dependable method handed over with enough generosity to let its next maker change it.

conditionalReadings.label: Family Craft in a Dependable Detail
conditionalReadings.description: Family craft can earn its reputation through a wick that burns steadily, a candle lasting the return journey, or a tool whose sound handle does not fail underground. Such small achievements have an audience that understands exactly what went right. A gift of good wax can show more attention to a chandler than another glittering trinket. conditionalReadings.label: Inherited Craft with a Household Audience
conditionalReadings.description: A plain dwelling can conceal shell mosaics, carved coral, stone designs, and delicate seaweed hangings whose makers have little interest in displaying them to a passing trader. Family teaching preserves the patient techniques behind that beauty. The person who exchanges goods tersely on the shore may have lavished attention on a familiar household's interior. Craftsmanship has an intimate audience: those who remember who taught the design, recognize a difficult carving, and live among the finished work. Useful skill and private beauty belong together even when outsiders assume that everything worth making must be offered for sale.

conditionalReadings.label: A Well-Made Brew Worth Sharing
conditionalReadings.description: Making and sharing alcoholic drink belong to everyday sociability and festivities, with brewing skill and local recipes held in esteem. Partaking is not required of every member. Brewing deserves the attention given to an art: ingredients chosen with curiosity, timing watched with patience, and a recipe made excellent enough to share. Regional brews and unfamiliar flavors can draw a traveler far from the shao'din whose companions know the maker best. The shared cup gives that wandering knowledge a home among friends. Enjoyment does not cancel discipline; care is what makes the evening worth enjoying. A new method can delight a teacher or wound the pride of one who mistakes difference for carelessness. An excellent brew means more when the maker remembers who has been waiting to taste it. Eligible city holdings may build the brewery line through this custom. Farm-and-field and manor-house lines add county approval where the local culture retains the enabling practice.

conditionalReadings.label: Strength Measured by Care for Vulnerability
conditionalReadings.description: Care for vulnerable people measures strength through what it sustains. In lean times, feeding the young and old before able adults makes generosity a cost somebody actually bears. An elder without surviving relatives still deserves shelter and a place among familiar voices. The adopted charitable ideal extends that concern beyond one's own kin and beliefs: a stranger's need does not become unreal because no shared ancestor can be named. There is dignity in helping someone remain part of life, whether through provisions, patient attention, or room at a gathering. A benefactor's pride is tested when the recipient cannot repay the favor.

conditionalReadings.label: Food as Accomplishment and Companionship
conditionalReadings.description: Food is both an art and a customary shared ceremony around which family and community gather; skilled preparation earns esteem beyond nourishment. Preparing food is an accomplishment with companions as its audience. A recipe asks for patient attention, a willingness to learn from unfamiliar ingredients, and the good sense to admit when an experiment has failed. A meal can give a traveler something learned abroad to offer the shao'din at home. Delight belongs in the taste and in the company, rather than only in winning praise for the cook. Friendship gives skill obligations: remembering another's preference, making room for a guest, or finishing the work before the conversation begins. A different method can be worth learning without dishonoring the one a teacher passed down. Feasts cost more; successful ones can earn extra prestige and dynasty renown. conditionalReadings.label: Discipline that Leaves Room for Delight
conditionalReadings.description: Body, breath, and attention are trained together as disciplines of character. Anger and grief are allowed their place, but endlessly feeding a feeling lets it command the person who thought to master it. Patient practice makes room between that appetite and the next choice. The ideal can accommodate a fine brew, an affectionate laugh, and an honest admission of failure; banishing every pleasure is another way to remain obsessed with control. A teacher's composure is tested by a pupil's unfamiliar method as surely as by danger. Discipline has succeeded when delight no longer requires everyone else to obey.

conditionalReadings.label: Gryphon Partnership
conditionalReadings.description: Falconry takes the Wildhammer form of raising gryphons and earning the trust of a powerful flying hunter. Those drawn to the calling learn fledgling care, mountain roosts, weather, and the country below a flight; riding is an honored partnership. A broad beak lowering toward a familiar hand and restless wings settling beside a trusted companion express a confidence that remains selective. The same gryphon may be gentle with its rider and dangerous to a stranger, with territorial instincts and an inconvenient appetite for horse flesh. A good rider listens when a partner refuses a landing or turns toward home. Care before and after flight sustains the bond beyond the boast of a daring crossing. Shared roost duties and provisioning for nesting gryphons make care a concern of the wider clan, including those who do not ride.

conditionalReadings.label: A Welcome Worth Remembering
conditionalReadings.description: Rulers are expected to welcome anyone who comes to their court generously and make hospitality a spectacular accomplishment. A magnificent welcome makes success visible and gives friends a share in the triumph. Expense, clever presentation, and useful introductions can advertise the host's connections while expressing real affection. The goblin who remembers exactly what a guest wants has understood more than the price of the gift. Excess can be exuberant: the point is partly that everyone should witness what the giver has managed to do. Yet hospitality has a revealing cost when the next bid offers a profit that would spoil the welcome. Giving generously can remain a source of pride even when the guest brings delight rather than a commercial return.
conditionalReadings.guard: Esteemed hospitality remains welcome as a virtue, not a fraudulent sales technique. No family-enterprise contributor, feast, guest, expenditure or fortune is required.

conditionalReadings.label: Family Enterprise with Costly Loyalties
conditionalReadings.description: A family enterprise ties wages, cargoes, designs, debts, and reputation to people who remember one another before the latest success. A carefully chosen gift can be affectionate and advertise excellent connections; an introduction can recognize a relative's talent while earning the introducer a share. Promises matter because the next customer and the next generation may both know who failed to deliver. Loyalty has a price the family understands precisely when a rival offers a tempting opportunity at another member's expense. Cleverness wins admiration, but success becomes richer when someone has earned a value that a higher bid cannot simply replace. Close relatives serving on councils or in court positions gain advantages in their work; revoking close kin's titles costs public prestige. This establishes no actual appointment, personal competence or title.

conditionalReadings.label: Female Standing with an Inward Audience
conditionalReadings.description: Female predominance has an inward audience as well as an outward claim to authority. Familiar voices in a nest remember who captured the admired prize, who received the richest spoils, and whose boast a matriarch publicly dismissed. Approval, envy, and fear make standing something repeatedly defended. An ornament displayed beyond another's reach can announce prestige as sharply as an order. Shared reputation can inspire pride in belonging while making ridicule from a companion particularly dangerous. The customary hierarchy shapes ordinary expectations and inheritance, but authority still depends on relationships among women whose ambitions need not agree. conditionalReadings.label: A Small Flame on the Sacred Way

conditionalReadings.label: Making Room for Life to Continue
conditionalReadings.description: Constructing, protecting, and helping something flourish are sources of virtue. Hakkar devotion can make that endurance a claim to chosen greatness while promises of favor remain painfully deferred. Alongside it, elemental-subjugation teaching demands that resistant land and elements yield to will. Service to a demanding power and mastery over nature give devotion different directions: the Soulflayer is not made an obedient elemental merely because the people seek to command the land. Approval can sustain magnificent confidence while impatience and dread persist beneath it. Neither commitment guarantees fulfillment, successful compulsion or agreement about the cost of continuing.
conditionalReadings.guard: Requires both independently affirmed Hakkar and elemental-subjugation teachings plus current Unrelenting. Hakkar's demands remain a service relationship rather than being reclassified as a commanded elemental.

conditionalReadings.label: The Promise Still Demands More
conditionalReadings.description: The faithful are praised for refusing surrender despite poor odds, remaining ready to fight or die. Magnificent confidence can carry impatience and dread when continued service has not settled what fulfillment would require. Neither striving nor favored standing guarantees that the demanding power will be satisfied.

conditionalReadings.label: No Final Yield
conditionalReadings.description: Conviction is praised for remaining ready to fight or die rather than surrender, even against poor odds. With Cult of Strength adopted, unceasing struggle and daily growth are held to draw the faithful toward divinity. Elemental-subjugation teaching makes that demand face resistant land and elements, whose compliance is sought through compulsion rather than willing partnership. A moment's apparent advantage would not release the devotee from the demand to keep growing. Pride in endurance can sit beside unease about a struggle that offers no final measure of enough. Resolve does not prove successful mastery, and the sacred demand grants no follower an actual power to command nature.

Service to the Soulflayer and attempted command of nature remain different relations. A devotee can take pride in endurance while wondering whether greater strength will ever satisfy either demand. No shared deity or promised final mastery resolves that tension. The ideals remain strong without proving personal power, a completed offering or unanimous willingness to bear the cost.

Discipline and resolve can matter alongside force when a devotee considers what continued resistance asks of the people. Boasting of mastery leaves the harder question of whether today's strength can answer tomorrow's demand. Perseverance can sustain pride while making release from the struggle difficult to imagine. conditionalReadings.label: The Purse and the Goods in Use
conditionalReadings.description: Consumption is held to be good in itself, with more goods acquired and used praised for widening cities and advancing society. Affirmed confidence in tangible profit gives value the test of what can be seen, used or spent: a filled purse promises influence, while goods put into use display what that influence accomplishes. A dazzling purchase can win recognition and still leave its usefulness disputed. Loyalty or generosity can cost profit without becoming unthinkable. This worldly confidence does not turn an inherited word for fortune into a literal god; any independently adopted worship must speak through its own current teaching. The ideal establishes neither the community's actual wealth nor a particular believer's greed, profession or purchase.

Holy Light teaching joins self and world through sensation, emotion and action. Respect, tenacity and wise compassion ask whether help serves another life; unwanted help can obstruct its growth. Neither private absorption nor self-erasure completes that connection. An empty purse can free attention for another life, but praise for purity can be hoarded as carefully as gold. Light teaching asks what the simpler devotee can offer and what care they can hear received. Shunning acquisition need not deny the self's worth or make another person's refusal an injury to one's virtue. The adopted norm retains its demand even when a believer weighs the comfort and responsibility that provision can bring. conditionalReadings.label: The Cup and the Dish Keep Their Methods
conditionalReadings.description: Making and sharing alcoholic drink belong to everyday sociability and festivities, with brewing skill and local recipes held in esteem. Partaking is not required of every member. Food is both an art and a customary shared ceremony around which family and community gather; skilled preparation earns esteem beyond nourishment. A cup's unfamiliar flavor may invite a recipe learned abroad, while a dish asks what heat and preparation brought an ingredient to its best use. Shao'din companions can remember the maker before either work won praise. Pairing drink and food deserves curiosity without making one method answer for the other; a carefully chosen pupil can earn trust by noticing the difference rather than copying the teacher's boast. Social etiquette is valued above all else, and accomplished diplomacy receives strong public esteem. The attentive welcome can take the form of a meal as readily as an explanation or a household adaptation. An unfamiliar preparation may solve the guest's small difficulty, while remembering a familiar preference can matter more than proving the maker ingenious. A companion can question a shortcut because they share the cook's hopes, and a graceful answer can keep that disagreement inside warm company. Etiquette gives the exchange strong standing without requiring every listener to like the recipe or every host to become an engineer. Feasts cost more; successful ones can earn extra prestige and dynasty renown. Eligible duchy-or-higher rulers may appoint a Food Taster; an appointee of this culture can perform better. Children more often develop Charming, and diplomacy-focused education can improve. Personal schemes can gain effectiveness, while hostile schemes against members also gain an advantage. Travel safety and court-grandeur growth can improve.

conditionalReadings.label: The Present Remembers Its Recipient

Social etiquette is valued above all else, and accomplished diplomacy receives strong public esteem. An inventive present can give an ordinary occasion extravagant recognition, but the graceful welcome remembers who must receive it. A joke understood, an overlooked achievement noticed or a generous explanation can make the display affectionate rather than merely impressive. Longstanding guests may find a place among household company without being asked to match its loudest enthusiasm. Exuberance can retain its public delight while etiquette makes room for an inconvenient answer; admiration for cleverness does not settle whether the gift served its recipient. A giver who keeps directing its use may want appreciation to become continuing influence. Eligible feasts and camp parties can recur sooner; reveler lifestyles are more common and carry added public prestige. Children more often develop Charming, and diplomacy-focused education can improve. Personal schemes can gain effectiveness, while hostile schemes against members also gain an advantage. conditionalReadings.label: Elekk Prestige and Patient Husbandry
conditionalReadings.description: Mighty elekk carry the royal prestige of this great-beast tradition. Capturing, training and caring for them, including their use in war, earn esteem through patient handling; a ruler's display depends on keepers whose work continues after the crowd leaves. No personal mount, office or handling skill follows.
conditionalReadings.guard: Current GoA draenei, Lightforged and Broken source cultures adopt Lords of the Elephant. GoA exarch_flavor explicitly describes draenei riding mighty elekk into battle; this gives their inherited great-beast tradition a concrete local expression. Royal esteem and husbandry come from the actual adopted tradition. Scope remains current/parent native culture plus actual adoption, including renamed or mixed descendants. conditionalReadings.label: Swift Tribal Warfare and Horsecraft
conditionalReadings.description: Centaur tribes prize swift movement in war: route knowledge, endurance and well-secured equipment help warriors choose where to strike or withdraw. Care of legs and hooves supports that mobility. Horse handling is also esteemed when riding is practiced; the custom establishes neither a person's body nor a present mount or personal skill.
